**Surah Ha Mim 'Ayn Sin Qaf**, also called **'Ayn Sin Qaf** and **Ash-Shura** (The Consultation).

Consultation requires that all the people of the religion be equal in it, just as they are equal in servitude to its Lawgiver. The greatest benefit in this is spending and sharing what is in one's hand, pardoning and overlooking the wrongs of the one who does evil, and submitting to the truth even when it is hard and burdensome. The book that calls to all of this is the spirit of the body of this religion. It expresses what it calls to of noble deeds and excellent qualities, by way of the Straight Path. To this the end of the preceding surah hinted, so that it would become clear to them that it is the truth: ﴿Is it not that He encompasses all things?﴾ [Fussilat: 54]. The surah explicitly stated what is in this one, in His words: ﴿Establish the religion and do not be divided therein﴾ [Ash-Shura: 13]; ﴿except affection toward the near relatives﴾ [Ash-Shura: 23]; ﴿Respond to your Lord﴾ [Ash-Shura: 47]; ﴿We guide by it whom We will of Our servants﴾ [Ash-Shura: 52]; ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [Ash-Shura: 52]; ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah all matters are returned﴾ [Ash-Shura: 53].

Likewise its naming by the disjoined letters, for they combine the three places of articulation: the throat, the lips, and the tongue. Likewise (p-231) their combining of the two categories, the dotted and the undotted letters, and the two qualities, the voiced and the voiceless. This is the agreement at the beginning. As for the agreement at the end, it is that the two surahs conclude with two words: the first of each of them is the last of the other, and the last of each is the first of the other. This indicates that the two surahs are one circle encompassing the religion, connected without any break. This is because the end of Maryam is the beginning of Ash-Shura, and the end of Ash-Shura is the beginning of Maryam: ﴿So We have only made it easy in your tongue﴾ [Maryam: 97], to the end of the verse. Allah is the Guide. Likewise, its naming by part of it, by the indication of the part upon the whole: "In the name of Allah" (*bismillah*), who encompassed the attributes of perfection, so His command took effect, and everything responded to Him, willingly or unwillingly. "The Most Merciful" (*ar-Rahim*), who specified His allies with what the Divinity is pleased with of His mercy, so He gathered their word upon His religion in belief, in action, and in outcome.

**Ha Mim 'Ayn Sin Qaf.** These letters may be allusions to words combined in a great discourse, indicating that the meaning of this combination may be stated as: "The wisdom of Muhammad (ﷺ) rose high and became general, so it healed the diseases of the hearts." Its letters were divided into two parts, in agreement with its sister surahs. After them come two verses. The letters of ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾ [Maryam: 1] were not divided, because it is a single verse with no sister. The letters of ﴿Alif Lam Mim Sad﴾ [Al-A'raf: 1] were not divided, for example, although it has sisters, because it is a single verse. No single letter in the Qur'an counts as a verse. It is also possible to consider the letters individually, and then they are allusions to secrets that fill the regions and expand the breasts and thoughts. If you look at their places of articulation, you will find that the beginning in them was from the lowest middle of the throat toward the tongue, with the name of *ha* (ح). It then curved to the middle letter of the lips, which is *mim* (م). Then it returned to the middle of the throat, from its farthest point on the tongue, with the name of *'ayn* (ع), which combines the throat and the tongue. Fourthly, it proceeded to the tongue with *sin* (س), which is from its lowest part to the lips, its tip, and it has contact with the two lips and connection to the upper part of the mouth. So in it, by this consideration, there is a combination. Then, after this manifestation, it made hidden depths (*buṭun*) toward the root of the tongue, which is its farthest point from the lips, with *qaf* (ق). The name of this letter has a combination: it begins at the root of the tongue with the roof of the throat, and concludes with the upper lip and the two lower incisors. So in these letters there are three which are the majority, and it is given consideration by what is in them of combination toward the aim of the surah. The beginning was harmonious in what consisted of two letters whose place of articulation combined them, first the higher and then the lower, as an indication that the people of this religion will have, after manifestation, hidden depths, just as at the beginning of Islam, when the Prophet (ﷺ) and his relatives were confined in the Shi'b (the valley of Abu Talib). This is also an indication that from the adornment of the outward one moves to the purification of the inward. Whoever adorns his outward with the gathering of righteous deeds, Allah purifies his inward through sincere and advising vigilance. Moreover, in this descent there is good news that the second state will be higher than the first, as it was at the emergence from the Shi'b, through the breaking of the unjust document, the tightness of which had been the cause of it. This is because the second of these letters' levels is stronger in quality than what is higher than it in articulation. *Ha* (ح) has among its qualities whispering (*hams*), softness (*rakhawa*), lowering (*istifal*), and openness (*infitah*). *Mim* (م) has among its qualities voicing (*jahr*), openness, lowering, and a state between firmness (*shidda*) and softness. *'Ayn* (ع) has the same qualities as *mim*. *Sin* (س) has the same qualities as *ha*, and it adds sibilance (*safir*). *Qaf* (ق) has among its qualities voicing, firmness, openness, elevation (*isti'la'*), and echo (*qalqala*). So the first letter has the most qualities of weakness, and it increases by the inclination (*imala*) which many reciters recite. The second and third are equal, and both are slightly more inclined toward strength. This is as was previously mentioned, the state of the middle at the exit from the Shi'b. The fourth has strength and weakness in it, and its weakness is greater, for it has three qualities of weakness and two of strength. This is like the condition of the Prophet (ﷺ) at the end of his affairs in blessed Makkah, when the two supporters, Khadija (may Allah be pleased with her) and Abu Talib, died. However, perhaps the two strong qualities were higher than the weak qualities, by what is in them of spreading through sibilance and gathering, which the indication has passed over, from the indication to a great multitude that would be formed by the gathering of helpers, as occurred in the Pledge of the Ansar. The fifth, which is the last, is entirely strength, as occurred after the Hijra, when the word was united and greatness became manifest. As the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"When we emigrated, we gained the upper hand over the people, and the turns of war were between us and them." Then strength was perfected at the perfection of unity, after fighting the people of apostasy (*ahl al-ridda*) after his death (ﷺ). Undoubtedly, the people of this religion spread across the earth to the right and to the left. No opponent stood against them, and no nation agreed with them, despite their weakness and fewness and the strength and multitude of others, without their (the others) being destroyed and made like yesterday's dwellings. These letters have been combined, as has passed, with the two qualities of voiced and voiceless. The voiced ones were the majority, an indication of the manifestation of this religion over every religion, as the reality of existence has verified. And with the two categories of dotted and undotted: all of them were undotted except for one letter. This is an indication that the best state of the believer is that the majority of his states be effacement, such that no quality of his is seen, rather he is counted among the dead. It is also an indication that those adorned with pure righteous deeds, among the people of the hearts from the possessors of this religion, are very few. The dotted letter was the last of them, an indication that the ultimate of levels for the people of truth is gathering after effacement and distinction. The letter of the lips among them was *mim*, which has the shape of a perfectly level circle, an indication that the people of this religion have, in gathering upon it, in conforming to it, in encircling it, and in hastening to it, what others do not have. And an indication that they have, from the firm step in the saying that is cut off from the mouth and concluded by the two lips, what no one else can reach, to the extent that it has no end, (p-236) together with the goodness of its radiance in harmony with its circularity. Then, when you reach the completion of the gathering in these letters, by adding up the numerical values of their names, which is two hundred and seventy-eight, and in the year corresponding to this number was my birth, then the beginning of this religious book at that time was with a potential close to actuality, and the year of my beginning in it in actuality was the year sixty-one (AH), in Sha'ban, when I was approaching fifty-four years of age. This corresponds to a numerical value of letters that enjoined an aspect of the religion, which is the aim of the surah. It was as if He commanded at that time the start of the book so that its aim would be achieved. The year of my arrival at this surah, which is the year seventy-one (AH), in Sha'ban of it, I was approaching sixty-four years of age, and this is a number corresponding to the number of the letters of "religion" (*din*), which is the aim of the surah. So I hope, by this remarkable coincidence, that this is an indication that Allah, exalted is He, will gather through this book of mine, which He singled me out to receive by His inspiration, and which He has stored up for me as a gift by its untying and its binding, its embracing and its adherence, the people of this upright religion, a great, noble, and magnificent assembly, in which there will appear a far-reaching effect in their unity and their fine emulation of its transmitters and followers' leaders. Among the noble effects, in its consideration for the gathering: since the aim of Surah Maryam (peace be upon her) was to explain the attribute of the Most Merciful, who sent down this Qur'an, of the comprehensiveness of mercy for all existence, and this surah was for a particular mercy, one of the effects of that general mercy, which is the gathering upon this religion whose manifestation and supremacy over every religion and whose subjugation of every matter is intended, therefore it was, for this reason, encompassing and overpowering the portion of every overpowering and oppressive one. This particular mercy was, in relation to the creation, secondary to that general one and branching from it. It was, because it is among the attributes of the creation, in the position of the left, and that one, because it is among the attributes of the Truth, in the position of the right. For this reason, Allah knows best, the Ustadh Abu al-Hasan al-Harali said in a book of his on the letters: "When that, namely this name composed of these disjoined letters, was the beginning of this surah, from what is ascribed to the matter of the left, whenever it was placed on the fingers of the left, then it was placed upon the mark of injustice or oppression, it overpowered it by the judgment of the encompassing wisdom of Allah. Its fifth was added to the fifth of *Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad* [Maryam: 1], which overpowers the wisdom of the right, this encompassing that by the tenth, which encompasses all the wisdom, whose support is the *ya* (ي), which is the first of the tenth and the place of balance, with what returns as the unity of the *alif*." End of quotation.

﴿Thus﴾ [as in the verse, Allah reveals to you, Muhammad, and to those before you]. Since these letters, Allah knows best, point to the gathering (of the message and its people), as the end of the previous surah indicated, Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Thus﴾, that is, in the same manner as this great revelation, which your Lord has explicitly informed you of at the beginning of Fussilat, namely that God is one God, and at its end, namely that nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you. It also points to Him gathering your community upon this religion, by making clear to them that this Qur'an is the truth, through the signs and clear proofs He shows them on the horizons and within themselves, and through His testimony, glorified be He, to the inimitability of the Qur'an for all of mankind and the jinn. This is especially so when a misguided person attempts to oppose it, as Musaylima did, for then the matter becomes clear to them with the utmost clarity, "and by their opposites things are made manifest." He, glorified be He, also signalled to you allusively at the beginning of this surah through these disjoined letters, which are higher and more precious than set jewels, and so on. Thus there are two kinds of revelation: the explicit and expressed, and the allusive and indicative.

Since the aim is comprehension, and since revelation from Him, glorified be He, is a continuous practice toward all His prophets and messengers, and a good tiding to him (ﷺ) that it will be renewed for him throughout his life, to steady his heart and to show the continuance of His affection, He used the present tense, which indicates renewal and continuity. It was mentioned at the beginning of al-Baqara, citing Abu Hayyan, and before him al-Zamakhshari and others, that the present tense may not be tied to a specific time, but rather intends pure existence. Thus He said: ﴿is revealed to you﴾, that is, in the past and in the future, for as long as you are alive, this will never be cut off from you at all, neither as farewell nor as displeasure, by what He wills of His command, which raises your rank, spreads your lights and elevates your beacon.

Since attention to the revelation is for knowing that it is true, as the reading of Ibn Kathir with the passive voice indicates, and attention to the one to whom it is revealed is for knowing that he is truly a messenger, and since the intended sense of the present tense is merely the occurrence of its meaning and does not indicate the future, it is valid for the phrase ﴿and to those who﴾, placed before the subject, to be connected to it. In Ibn Kathir's reading, the element standing in place of the subject is a pronoun referring back to ﴿thus﴾.

Since the messengers are among those who preceded in some periods of the past, He introduced the preposition, saying ﴿before you﴾, that is, from among the noble messengers and the eminent prophets, indicating that your community is the most numerous of nations and that you are the most noble of the prophets. He took from each of them a covenant to follow you and to be among your supporters and partisans.

Since He placed first what is most important, namely the revelation and the one to whom it is revealed, He then brought the subject of ﴿reveals﴾ in the reading of the majority, saying ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses the comprehensive attributes of perfection. In Ibn Kathir's reading it is in the nominative, governed by a hidden verb whose implied sense is "the One who reveals it." Since the execution of command revolves around might and wisdom, He said ﴿the Mighty﴾, that is, the One who overcomes everything and is not overcome by anything, ﴿the Wise﴾, who places what He does in the most perfect of its places. For this reason, none can overturn what He has decreed, nor diminish what He has made firm.

Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: Since the surah of Ghafir contained what has preceded of the explanation of the states of the obstinate and the deniers, and since it was followed by the surah of al-Sajda, explaining that the state of the unbelievers of the Arabs in this matter is like the state of those who preceded them, and clarifying that this is the Mighty Book whose proof is great, yet they did not find (guidance) for those whom Allah, exalted be He, had decreed for disbelief, the two surahs were followed by what al-Shura contains: that all of this happened only in accordance with what was foreknown in His knowledge, exalted be He, by the judgment of eternity: ﴿a party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze﴾ [al-Shura: 7], ﴿and you are not responsible for them﴾ [al-Shura: 6], ﴿and if Allah had willed, He would have made them one community﴾ [al-Shura: 8], ﴿and had it not been for a prior word, they would have been judged between﴾ [al-Shura: 21], ﴿and He is able to gather them when He wills﴾ [al-Shura: 29], ﴿and you cannot escape on earth﴾ [al-Shura: 31], ﴿and whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no way﴾ [al-Shura: 46], ﴿your duty is only to convey﴾ [al-Shura: 48], ﴿by it We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. So reflect on these and what is joined to them, of which little has occurred in the preceding surah, and the firm structure of what it draws in, and the structure of this surah (p-241) rests on that, and its verses revolve around it. The connection of this surah to what precedes it and its joining to what is adjacent to it becomes evident to you.

When the surah of al-Sajda ended with His saying, exalted be He, ﴿Unquestionably, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord﴾ [Fussilat: 54], He followed it, glorified be He, with declaring Himself far above their doubt and their suspicion, saying, exalted be He, ﴿The heavens are almost splitting apart from above them﴾ [al-Shura: 5], just as He followed with a similar statement in His saying, exalted be He, ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son."﴾ [Maryam: 88] ﴿You have certainly produced something monstrous﴾ [Maryam: 89] ﴿The heavens are almost splitting apart from it﴾ [Maryam: 90]. And since the mention of the arrogance of the polytheists and their distance from submission was repeated in the surah of Ha Mim al-Sajda, in His saying, exalted be He, ﴿but most of them turned away﴾ [Fussilat: 4] ﴿and they say, "Our hearts are in coverings"﴾ [Fussilat: 5], along with what He, exalted be He, mentioned of their condition, which indicates their remoteness from accepting, He said, exalted be He, in the surah of al-Shura: ﴿Difficult for the polytheists is that to which you call them﴾ [al-Shura: 13]. End.

Since He, glory be to Him, has informed us that He is always the one who sends down revelation of the laws, both in the past and in the present, He explained this by stating that He is the possessor of universal dominion, saying: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens﴾, that is, of essences and meanings, ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾, likewise. Since loftiness entails power, He said: ﴿And He is the Most High﴾, that is, above the Throne, in which the heavens are contained, a loftiness of rank, greatness and station, not of place or contact. Thus it follows that all the heavens and all the earths, together with what is in them, belong to Him. ﴿The Most Great﴾, that is, nothing can be imagined in the mind or conceived in the intellect except that He is greater than it in subjugation and dominion. Therefore He reveals to whomever He wills whatever He wills, whether confirmation or abrogation, and no one has any objection against Him.

[p. 242] Since the context conveys the greatness of His dominion and power, glorified is He, through the multitude of bodies and meanings in the cosmos, which, given their magnitude, cannot be borne, He said, explaining this: ﴿The heavens are almost rent asunder﴾, meaning, given the greatness of their creation, the firmness of their origination, and their being split by what He has made known of the occurrence. He drew attention to it by the masculine form of ﴿are almost﴾ in the recitation of Nafi' and al-Kisa'i (the canonical reading, qira'a), ﴿rent asunder﴾, meaning they split open, and their parts break apart entirely (infitar mutlaq), in the recitation of the one who recited with the nun and lightened the letter, and they here are Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub, and Shu'ba from 'Asim. And the recitation of the rest, with the taa' at the top, open, and the taa' doubled, is "to split apart severely" (tafattur shadid), beginning with ﴿from above them﴾, which by custom is harder than what is beneath it, so the splitting of what is other than it is a fortiori. The beginning of the splitting is from there because the direction of above is more fitting for the manifestation of what is too heavy to bear of the great majesty, magnificence, grandeur, and might, among which is what the angels carry, whose minds cannot contain their description, given the great size of each one of them in form, height, sturdiness, and bigness, and other things that none knows fully except He who sees them, to such an extent that if one of them is pointed to the earth he would carry it, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The heaven groans, and it has the right to groan; there is not a space of four fingers in it where there is not an angel standing and praying." And other than that of the greatness, grandeur, majesty, and sublimity. Or their splitting may be from the enormity of the abomination of disbelief in the One who created the earth in two days and made for Him equals, as He said in the sura parallel to this one, the sura of Maryam: ﴿The heavens are almost rent from it, and the earth is split asunder, and the mountains fall down in ruin﴾ [Maryam 19:90] ﴿that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son﴾ [Maryam 19:91]. What is in this is less than that, because it does not mention the child here. This is an allusion to warning of punishment, because it is known that when the high thing splits, it becomes ready to fall, and when it falls, it destroys what is beneath it. How much more so when it is of such height, magnitude, and weight of body, in a state that none encompasses except its Originator. So mentioning "above" is a depiction of the great calamities that follow from this splitting. On this basis it is good that the pronoun returns to the heavens that disbelieved in their Originator.

When he had explained that the cause of the near-splitting of them is the sublimity of the greatness, among which is the multitude of the angels, and the enormity of disbelief, he explained to them another cause, which is the immensity of their saying. He said: ﴿And the angels﴾, meaning and the state being that they, and he turned away from the feminine to the masculine out of regard for the wording, and the plural pronoun indicates the strength of glorification and the multitude of those who glorify, so He said: ﴿glorify﴾, meaning they bring about the declaring-Him-free-of-imperfection and sanctification of God, glorified is He and exalted, ﴿with the praise of their Lord﴾, meaning by affirming perfection for the One who does good to them, glorifying in a manner befitting what is theirs, by what the idafa (construct phrase) indicates, constantly, they never slacken. Thus they have a clamor and voices that minds cannot bear, and mountains cannot withstand them. So do not consider that unlikely, for how many a thunderbolt have I heard from the clouds, whereby the earth shook, and the sturdy structures and hard mountains were split by it. He turned the speech to the attribute of beneficence to praise the angels, by alluding to their having recognized the beneficence of the Beneficent and acting in thankfulness according to what His beneficence required. This becomes an indirect rebuke of the disbelievers for what they concealed of His beneficence and what they sought refuge in of ingratitude.

Since they, by their knowledge of the majesty of God, glorified is He, were shy before Him, glorified is He, as the people of the earth do, and they would not say what is not befitting of His lofty presence and His exalted court, and they knew from what He, glorified is He, had argued with them about them that He has care for them, they would see that the closest thing to His good pleasure was to seek forgiveness for them. For this reason He, glorified is He, expressed them by His saying, skillfully fitting what the context required in ﴿The Forgiver﴾ [Ghafir 40:3] of mention of faith, indicating that the closest of creation to the Throne is like the most distant of people in faith that depends on the unseen, in order to make the declaring-free-of-imperfection complete, because there is no requirement for it here: ﴿and they seek forgiveness﴾, meaning, and they with the glorification seek forgiveness ﴿for those on the earth﴾, because of what they see of the great shortfall of people in fulfilling the right of that greatness, which cannot be matched. As for the believer, it is absolute; as for the disbeliever, it is by postponing the requital; and likewise for the rest of the animals. That is because of what overwhelms them of what they witness of the greatness of the One of Majesty and the sublimity of the One of Might. Ibn Burjan said: God, whose remembrance is exalted, did not will the existence of anything without appointing angels from His servants who intercede for its existence, and likewise for the continuance of what He wills to continue and the annihilation of what He wills to annihilate. These are the foundations of intercession, so do not be among the doubters. More subtle than that is that the near-splitting of them is in a state of the angels' glorification and seeking forgiveness, because of what they see above them of greatness and below them of the sins of the two worlds (humans and jinn). Had it not been for their mention, they would have split, the punishment would have come, the creation would have been hastened to destruction, the Resurrection would have taken place, and the matter would have been decided. If the near-splitting occurs even with this glorification and seeking forgiveness, what then would happen if the matter were stripped of it and empty of it? For this reason He mentioned the generality here and did not specify the believers for forgiveness as in ﴿The Forgiver﴾ [Ghafir 40:3], because the context here requires generality, and because the intent of "The Forgiver" [p. 246] is the classification of people in the Hereafter into two categories and the full repayment of what each deserves, so it suited that the believers be singled out, who are characterized by faith, whereas the intent of this gathering is the religion in this world, so it suited that supplication be for all, so that each may be recompensed according to what he deserves: absolute forgiveness in both abodes for the believer, and its restriction to postponement in this world for the disbeliever.

Since the deeds and sayings of the people of the earth are greatly opposed to what pleases Him, glorified is He, and they deserve to be hastened to punishment because of them, He answered someone who seemed to say: "This is granted to them regarding the believers, so how is it granted to them regarding the disbelievers?" so that the speech would combine awe and dread at its beginning, and good tidings, kindness, and facilitation at its end. He said, turning the speech from the attribute of beneficence to the Greatest Name, to define the great matter, in order to bind one to praise and to perpetual thankfulness: ﴿Behold, indeed God﴾, meaning the One to whom belongs the comprehensiveness of the attributes of perfection, so to Him belongs all greatness, and He emphasized because such a thing, given its greatness, is hardly believed. ﴿He is﴾, meaning He alone, and He arranged His two attributes, glorified is He, in the highest forms of eloquence, beginning with what indicates the answering of the angels and following it with the announcement of increased honor, so He said: ﴿the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾, meaning the one of all-encompassing concealment and honor in the most eloquent manner. As for the people of faith, it is clear, in this world and the next. As for the people of disbelief, in this world He provides for them, gives them health, and gives them respite: ﴿And if God were to take people to task for what they have earned, He would not leave on its back a single creature﴾ [Fatir 35:45]. As for other than God, He does not forgive [p. 247] the people of His disobedience, and even if He wished that, He would not be able to.

Since the sense is: those who turned to Him (ولاه) and died in His guardianship, then He forgives their sins, meaning He removes them both in essence and in effect, He connected to it His saying: ﴿And those who take** ﴾, that is, who work upon their natural dispositions (fiṭar) and their intellects until they take, ﴿besides Him﴾, that is, from a rank lower than His rank, ﴿protectors﴾ whom they worship like idols, and everyone who follows his desire in any matter has taken Satan, who commands him to that, as a protector besides God by opposing His command.

Since what they did was of great abomination, the longing for their recompense became intense, so He, glorified be He, informed about it with His saying, expressing by the Greatest Name an indication of the clarity of their error and the magnitude of their threat, dropping the fa' from it lest it be imagined that the guarding is a consequence of the taking mentioned, and turning to the expression by the Name of Majesty (al-Jalalah) to magnify what is in polytheism of wrong and to intensify the rebuke deserved by its doer: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing the attributes of perfection, ﴿is Watcher over them﴾, that is, Overseer, Guardian and Witness over their deeds, from whose knowledge none of their conditions is absent. So if He wills, He keeps them upon their disbelief and recompenses them for it with what He has prepared for the disbelievers; and if He wills, He turns to them in repentance and erases that both in essence and in effect, so He does not punish them nor reproach them; and if He wills, He erases it in essence but leaves the trace until He reproaches them. ﴿And you are not over them a guardian﴾, that is, to the point that it obliges you to watch all their conditions, of their sayings and their actions, so that you preserve them and compel them to abandon them, and the like of that which the guardian undertakes on behalf of the one who appoints him, whether they say ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an﴾ [Fussilat: 26], or they say ﴿Our hearts are in coverings﴾ [Fussilat: 5], or other than that.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 7:

Since the earlier revelation at the beginning of the surah was (given) as good news, because it is the principal aim in itself, and since the good news required an allusion and a symbolic indication through the disjointed letters (al-ahruf al-muqatta'ah) to the gathering of the people of the religion (ahl al-din), their dominance over all other religions, that their religion encompasses all nations and embraces all creation, and that no one intends evil to its people without it bringing him elevation, as its explanation has already passed; and since it was symbolic because the context is one of warning (nidhar), as the preceding surah attests; and since its purpose is repetition so that its delight remains in the ear of the one who gives the good news and its sweetness in his heart, He mentioned it with the present tense (lafz al-mudari'), which indicates renewal, repetition, occurrence and continuity. The obstinate one might have been moved by it to demand a promise of revelation in the future, while the intelligent person is content with the warning once. So He said, expressing it with the past tense, which indicates execution, finality, and irrevocable decree, concerning both the revelation and its benefit, which is warning, joining it to what is connected with the preceding verse, which ends with the negation of guardianship (wikalah), the implied meaning of which is: "Your duty is only to convey, with good tidings and warning. We have indeed revealed to you the good news in symbolic form, as is the custom of loved ones in their address-dialogues." He turned the speech to the locus of majesty, because warning is among its functions:

﴿And thus﴾ i.e., and like that revelation which We have just mentioned, with which We have granted you the revelation of the indication through the disjointed letters, ﴿We have revealed﴾ by virtue of Our majesty, with the distinction from every (other) ambiguity, ﴿to you a Qur'an﴾ comprehensive of every wisdom, ﴿Arabic﴾, so it is clear in address, evident in rightness, and inimitable in its sublimity, ﴿that you may warn﴾, i.e., by it, ﴿the Mother of Towns﴾, Makkah, which is the mother of the earth and its origin, from which it was spread out (Q. 79:30), and for its nobility the verb was applied to it, and it was given the status of rational beings. Then He explained that the intended ones are its people by His saying: ﴿and those around it﴾, i.e., and you warn those who are ﴿around it﴾, and they are the inhabitants of the whole earth, which is its mother. Al-Baghawi interpreted it thus, saying: "the towns of the earth, all of them," and likewise al-Qushayri, who said: "The world surrounds the Ka'bah and Makkah, for it is the navel of the earth."

Since the second object of "you warn" (tundhir), according to what the context indicates, is what the earlier nations and past generations were punished with, when disbelief overstepped its bounds and injustice prevailed over them in taking guardians besides Allah, He joined to it: ﴿and warn﴾, i.e., the Mother of Towns and those around it, along with the punishment of the nations in this world, ﴿of the Day of Assembly﴾, i.e., for all creatures, by their resurrection from death. He omitted the first object of the second clause and the second object of the first clause, so the verse is of the type of ihtibak (mutual omission): He mentioned the warners first, indicating their being intended in the second, and He mentioned the thing warned of, namely the Day of Assembly, in the second, indicating the thing warned of from the punishment of the nations in the first, so that the mind may go in the omitted part every way, and it becomes more awesome. The mention of this that has been mentioned is more magnificent and more fearful.

Since warning, which is informing about the place of fear, is sometimes about what one has no knowledge of, which is the more common case, and sometimes about what one has acted upon, then the warned one contradicts his knowledge and acts as one who has no knowledge of it, He pointed out that this is of the second type by saying in a circumstantial clause: ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾, i.e., because it has been firmly established in the nature of every person that when a ruler employs his servants in something and then they wrong one another, he must, as governance requires, gather them so as to do justice between them, otherwise he would be considered foolish. So what do you think of the Most Wise of the wise?

Since the listener was eager to know what He would do with their assembly, and since the two species (al-thaqalan), by what they were created with of deficiency, were a people of division and transgression, He mentioned its outcome, expressing it with what belongs to division, saying, justifying the beginning with an indefinite noun for detailing or for establishing the attribute: ﴿a party﴾, i.e., of the two gathered groups, people of a division whom Allah overtook by making them people of unity (jam'), ﴿in the Garden﴾, out of His bounty, and they are those who accepted the warning and exerted themselves in caution; ﴿and a party﴾, i.e., of them, whom Allah forsook and left to themselves, so they increased in division, ﴿in the Blaze﴾, out of His justice. Al-Qushayri said: Just as in this world they are two groups: a group in the ranks of obedience and the sweetnesses of worship, and a group in the darkness of polytheism and the punishments of denial and doubt, so on the morrow they are two groups: a group who are the people of the encounter, and a group who are the people of affliction and misery.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us with two books in his hand, and said: 'Do you know what these two books are?' We said: 'No, unless you inform us, O Messenger of Allah!' He said to the one in his right hand: 'This is a book from the Lord of the worlds, with the names of the people of the Garden, the names of their fathers and their tribes; then it is summarized at the end of them, and nothing is added to them nor is anything taken from them, ever.' Then he said to the one in his left: 'This is the book of the people of the Fire, with their names and the names of their fathers and their tribes; then it is summarized at the end of them, nothing is added to them nor is anything taken from them, ever.' The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Then for what should we act, if this is a matter already concluded?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Be upright and draw near (to the mark), for the companion of the Garden is sealed with the deed of the Garden, however he may act; and the companion of the Fire is sealed with the deed of the Fire, however he may act.' He gestured with his hand and closed it, then said: 'Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has finished with the servants.' Then he said with his right hand and cast it away, saying: 'A party in the Garden,' and cast with his left and said: 'A party in the Blaze.'"

Ibn Kathir said: Thus did al-Nasa'i and al-Tirmidhi both narrate it, and al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih gharib."

When the kings of this world are dominant, they do not want their command to be disobeyed. If they warn against something, they want it not to be approached. If someone does it anyway, his act is outside their intention, so their punishment of him, because he has departed from what they intended, is a cure for the rage that has taken hold of them. He (glorified is He) showed that He is not like this. He is exalted above anything departing from His will, and above any benefit reaching Him through obedience or any harm through disobedience. His punishment is only for disobeying His command while being subject to His will by compulsion and coercion. This is the reality (fi nafs al-amr). Outwardly, however, the matter is that nothing appears to prevent either of these except the diversion of choice. So He said, turning the speech away from the locus of majesty, in order to complete the warning about what is truly deserving of it, to the Name that gathers the attributes of majesty and others, because the situation calls for it: ﴿And if God had willed﴾, that is, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, ﴿He would have made them﴾, that is, those gathered together, ﴿one community﴾, either for punishment or for reward. But He did not will that; rather He willed that they be two groups: those who act justly and those who are wrongdoers, so that His bounty and His justice would appear, and that He is the God, the Compeller, the One, the Subduer, who is not concerned with anyone. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿But He admits whom He wills﴾, that is, admitting him ﴿into His mercy﴾ by creating guidance in his heart, so that his actions are in their proper places, and these are the just. And He admits whom He wills into His vengeance by creating misguidance in their hearts, so that they become wrongdoers, and then no action of theirs falls in its proper place. Thus the just have no enemy and no one to object to them. ﴿But the wrongdoers﴾, that is, those who are deeply immersed in wrongdoing, whose wrongdoing He willed, so He admits them into His curse, ﴿have no protector﴾ who looks after their affairs and strives to set them right, ﴿nor any helper﴾ who gives them victory over humiliation. The verse is of the ihtibak (a rhetorical device of mutual omission, in which each part is left implicit and understood from the other). Its outward form: mention of mercy first is a sign of the curse second, and mention of wrongdoing and what accompanies it second is a sign of their opposites first. Its secret is that He mentioned the true cause regarding the people of happiness, so as to move them to greater gratitude, and the apparent cause regarding the people of wretchedness, so as to forbid them from disbelief.

(p-253)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 9:

Since the sense of the passage is: "Have those whom you warn, with their resolve, their intentions, their words and their deeds, restricted themselves to God Most High, taking admonition and heeding the warning by means of this inimitable speech?", he shifted to His saying ﴿Or have they taken﴾, that is, they have worked on their innate nature (fitrah), which testifies to this through the testimony of times of distress, until they turned it away from Him, the Glorified, and so they took ﴿protectors besides Him﴾, while knowing that these cannot benefit them at all. For this reason He said ﴿So God﴾, that is, He established as a consequence of what the form of the verb in the ifti'al pattern (the eighth verbal form, which implies taking something for oneself) indicated, namely that they know He alone is the one who harms and benefits, their knowledge (p-254) that ﴿He﴾ alone is ﴿the Protector﴾, and none other. It is also permissible that it is a consequence of this rhetorical interrogation of denunciation and reproof, as if it had been said: "Have they restricted their aspirations to Him, the Glorified?" So He established that He alone, and He alone praised, is the one deserving of what they intend of allegiance. ﴿And He﴾, likewise alone and none other, ﴿gives life to the dead﴾, that is, He renews their revival at whatever time He wills. ﴿And He﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿is Powerful over all things﴾, that is, of absolute power, and nothing shares with Him in that, as testified by every person of intellect. He emphasized this with the restrictive form (al-qasr), because their associating others with Him through protectors is a denial of His exclusive right to guardianship.

When they all acknowledged, in times of distress, everything that He described His holy Self as in this verse, some of it explicitly (the oneness of Lordship, giving life in this world, and power over everything), and some of it by necessary implication (giving life through resurrection), it follows with certainty that, while the speech shifts to direct address, there is an indication that He, the Exalted, brought every good close to them and brought the understanding of His oneness close to their minds, after He had created them with an innate disposition to hold to it when they are compelled. Therefore, whatever you agree upon concerning His command, glorified is He, is the truth. That is the foundation of the religion upon which all creatures unanimously agreed in times of compulsion, in which no weak person hesitated, nor any arrogant tyrant. He followed this with His saying (p-255) ﴿And whatever you differ about﴾, meaning, O creatures, ﴿concerning it, of any matter﴾, which refers to the branches in general and the foundations in a state of ease, ﴿its judgment is with Allah﴾, meaning the One who is the Protector and not other than Him, and who is the Capable and not other than Him, so nothing departs from His command. So investigate it, and you will find it in His Book, for in it is the clarification of everything. If your understandings fall short of extracting it from there, then seek it in the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ. If that is difficult for you, then seek it in the consensus (ijma', the agreement of the scholars) of the people of his religion. If that too is unavailable to you, then seek it through analogy (qiyas, reasoning by analogy) with something of that kind.

Al-Qushayri said: These matters are the canon of the Shari'ah, and its whole is from the Book of Allah, for the Book is what indicates the soundness of this whole. End of quote.

And whatever you have striven to understand regarding what He legislated for you, and distinguished by what has become apparent to you, according to the wisdoms of exerting effort (ijtihad, independent legal reasoning), has passed. As for what is not decided among you, glorified is He, on this Day, if He wills, by granting victory to the one who is right and abandonment to the wrongdoer; and if He wills, He will defer it until the Day of Judgment. Then if He wills, He will pardon, and if He wills, He will punish for it. There is no judgment for anyone other than Him, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

When this yielded the conclusion that there is no one greater than Him, and no god but Him, he expressed that by saying, addressing all: ﴿That is Allah﴾, meaning the One of exceedingly great rank, who encompasses all attributes of perfection, so He has no partner in any of it in any way, ﴿my Lord﴾, the One who has no other sustainer in past, present, or future. When that was the case, it necessarily yielded His saying: ﴿Upon Him I have relied﴾, meaning upon Him alone, ﴿I have submitted﴾, meaning I have surrendered (p-256) all my affairs, ﴿and to Him I turn back﴾, meaning not to other than Him, ﴿in repentance﴾, meaning I return in repentance whenever I fall short in some of the branches of His law, and I return to His Book whenever some matter befalls me, so I know its ruling from it. So you too, do likewise: make Him the judge, and you will prosper, and do not deviate from it in anything, or you will perish.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 11:

Having established through this discourse that He has implanted in the natural dispositions (fitra) that there is no deity other than Him, because He is the Creator of all else, as necessity guides to this even when wantonness makes one forget it, He described Himself with the proof for this, which all natural dispositions are created upon: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, the One who initiates them by creating and bringing them out of non-existence. Whatever you have taken as a protector besides Him is from them, and so it is among what He originated. As each of you knows this, none of you disputes it. This is the reason for the knowledge implanted in the natural dispositions, that He is the One with whom there is no deity, as He was in eternity, and nothing was with Him.

When He mentioned what split non-existence through His bringing into being without any cause at all, He followed it with what He caused from that, creating from the elements which the hand of power originated in the two regions (the heavens and the earth). He said, expressing it in the verbal form, to remind them of what obliges them to acknowledge what His Prophet (ﷺ) acknowledged, that He alone is their Lord, with no partner in that, and this obliges reliance upon Him alone: ﴿He made for you﴾, that is, after (p-257) He created you from the earth, ﴿from yourselves mates﴾, by which, through tranquility in them, your kind endures. Since the cattle and their benefits are for our sake, He said: ﴿and of﴾, that is, and He made for you from ﴿the cattle﴾, which are your wealth and camels, and through which your sustenance is greatly maintained, ﴿mates﴾, that is, from their own kind, by which too the continuation of their kind endures. The same applies to all animals. The meaning of His saying, giving precedence to rational beings: ﴿He multiplies you﴾, that is, He creates you and increases you. Since mates are in the utmost love for marriage, to the extent that it dominates the hearts, it was as if it encompassed them, so He said: ﴿therein﴾, that is, in that mating, in a way that makes you devoted to it, from His saying dharā, meaning He created it, multiplied it, and made it attached to a thing. Thus you have, in the mates among humans, offspring, beauty and childbearing, and in the cattle, food, drink, clothing, and other benefits you have from them. You will continue in this manner of creation and mating, generation after generation and era after era.

Since it is established in minds and has become fixed in many intellects that nothing comes to be except by means of mating, it may have been that some of this illusion creeps into what concerns the Creator, glory be to Him. So He negated it in the most emphatic way by His saying, as a resumed statement answering one who asks about Him: ﴿Not﴾. He placed the predicate first because what is intended is negation of it. The negating particle has priority, indicating intense care for His own self. So He said: ﴿like Him﴾, that is, like (p-258) His very self, in His essence or in any of His attributes: ﴿anything﴾ that mates with Him or is similar to Him. Whatever you have taken as a protector besides Him has what mates with it and resembles it. Here, therefore, mithl (likeness) means the self (nafs), and this is its original and literal meaning, from the expression mithl al-rajul yumaththilu, meaning when he stood up and became erect. The Imam ʿAbd al-Haqq al-Ishbili said in his book al-Wa'i: "The mathal may be the statement itself: ﴿The likeness (mathal) of the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised﴾ [Muhammad: 15], so its mathal is the report about it." It was also said: "The mathal here is the attribute: ﴿and when there has not yet come to you the likeness (mathal) of those who passed away before you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214], that is, their attribute." Al-Harawi related this, and related from Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Qazzaz his saying concerning: ﴿A likeness has been coined, so listen to it﴾ [al-Hajj: 73] likewise, because He said: ﴿Indeed those you invoke﴾ [al-Hajj: 73], and so the report about that became the mathal. He said: "It is, according to what we have mentioned, that the mithl of a thing is its attribute and its form." It is related from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read "mithal," and read "amthal al-Jannah allati waʿad al-muttaqun" (the likenesses of the Garden which the God-fearing were promised). Then he said: "All of this indicates that the meaning of mathal is an attribute and a form." Abu ʿAbd Allah said: "Mathalat lahu al-shay' tamthilan" means she depicted the thing for him until it was as if he were looking at it. In a hadith: "The Garden and the Fire were depicted (muththilat) to me." End of quote. In the Qamus: al-mithl, with a kasra and with fatha on the mim and with a damma (as in amr), means the likened one; al-mathal, with a fatha on the mim and the letter after it with a fatha, means the proof, the statement, and the attribute; al-mathil means the measure, retribution, and the attribute of a thing and of a bed, its plural being amthila and muthul; al-timthal, with a kasra, means the image. And mathal qa'iman: he stood erect, like mathal, without a damma, mathulan. End of quote. In Shams al-ʿUlum: the Arabs use mathal in the place of nafs, so they say: "Mithli does not say this," meaning "I do not say this." End of quote. It is thus clear that mathal, whether with sukun or with fatha, is one and the same, and that originally it is an expression for the very self and form of a thing, then it spread to what resembles it. So the meaning of mathth-a, that is, stood erect, took shape and was imagined, so that it had a form and shape, because by standing erect its form is realized and becomes manifest. Likewise mathal in the sense of clinging to the ground, though its manifestation is clearer by standing. Likewise mathal when it moves from its place, since erection or clinging has occurred, and movement is added. This is clarified by their saying: "Mathalahu lahu," when he depicted it until it was as if he were looking at it. Thus it is known with certainty that the meaning of the verse is what I have said. And if it had been said "﴿there is nothing like Him﴾" without the kaf (like), perhaps some of the quarrelsome people would say: "This means He is not a thing, because we know that mithl is the thing itself." They used to quarrel even without this, so He brought the kaf to remove this quarrel, together with the certain knowledge that the apparent meaning we understand is not intended, because it leads to two absurdities which are in the utmost weakness, and one who has even a little wisdom would be averse to either of them, so how about when both are combined? How about the Most Wise of the wise? One of them: that He has a likeness. The second: that His likeness has no likeness, along with the judgment that it is His likeness, and that is an evident contradiction. Allah is exalted far above intending His likeness, exceedingly high. And Allah is the Granter of success.

Since He, glory be to Him, had concealed His self by this declaration of transcendence with a great concealment, and since this profound hiddenness is not borne by the intellects, and they cannot be assured against inclining toward negation (ta'til), He brought Himself near by a kind of manifestation, by mentioning what we comprehend of attributes after safety from anthropomorphism for one who reflects on the speech, and the judgment of reason and the repelling of illusion. So He mentioned the clearest of what we perceive of our attributes and the most apparent of them, together with its implying the rest of the attributes. He said: ﴿And He﴾, that is, while the state is that there is no other than Him, ﴿is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾, that is, the perfect in hearing and seeing and knowledge, from sight and insight. It is certain that this does not occur in the specific way except with oneness, life, power, will and speech. So this verse fulfilled what the conjunction hinted at in His saying "and you did not differ" after it had expressed it explicitly. Thus Allah is the Protector, from the foundations of the religion, with the seven attributes in the most complete manner. And Allah is the Granter of success. Al-Harrali said: Hearing is the perception of the subtler of two likenesses, which is the name, and sight is the perception of the more manifest of two likenesses, which is the form. And with the Truth, glory be to Him, every subtle likeness begins. So He is the All-Hearing in reality, in that He does not hear what is the originator of a subtler likeness of it, or does not see what is the originator of a more manifest likeness of it. And since He, glory be to Him and exalted, is All-Knowing of the likenesses of things that begin before they exist, He is All-Hearing of them and All-Seeing of them before they exist. Only one who follows his knowledge with the perception of his senses acquires hearing and sight, not one who is always All-Hearing and All-Seeing of what He always knows. He, glory be to Him, hears things even if they have not been given a name, and sees them even if His seeing of them has not been imagined. His hearing in their creation and in their fashioning and shaping is a constant seeing and a constant hearing, while created beings do not see a thing before it is imagined, nor hear it before it is spoken. End of quote.

The verse has explicitly declared His transcendence above any equal in anything whatsoever. So whoever claims for anyone equality with Him in any of His attributes, whether knowledge or other, has associated that person with Him in that attribute. This is more blameworthy than associating a idol or the like of the created beings, because the association of the latter is clearly a delusion and evidently a flaw, manifestly base, while the association of the former is hidden and only the firmly grounded can untie it, though each of them ends in feebleness and nonsense. For no intellect allows that one person be a partner of another in anything unless he is equal to him in the very reality of essence, and suitable in general to take his place in all attributes. So beware, then beware, of a slip by which Satan has often misled some who wish to rise in the degrees of gnosis, in order to take him out of all religions.

When he had established the matter of revelation through the inimitability (*i'jaz*) by which it is proven, and had shown them the signs on the horizons, [showing] that to Him belongs what is in existence and that He is the One who originated it, and since it may be that a person possesses something without having full control over it, such as when the keys to its treasuries are shared with a partner or someone else, and a person may invent a building that belongs to another, He informed, as a completion of the purification (*tanzih*) in the preceding verse and an explanation of it, that (p-٢٦٢) He, exalted is He, is not like anything, as He is not like others in this matter either. Rather, just as to Him belongs what is in the two realms (*al-khafiqayn*), and He is their originator, so to Him are the keys to their treasuries. So He said: ﴿To Him﴾, that is, to Him alone, ﴿belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, their treasuries and the keys to their treasuries, of rain, plant growth, and other things. It is established that He originated them, and that to Him belongs everything in them, including what they have taken as protectors apart from Him and other things. Al-Qushayri said: "The *maqalid* (keys) are the treasuries, and His treasuries are His decrees." End of quotation.

Since He had restricted the matter to Himself, He indicated this by His saying: ﴿He extends provision﴾, that is, what is in them, and nothing prevents it except His power, ﴿for whomever He wills﴾, that is, to extend it to him, ﴿and He restricts it﴾, that is, He narrows and withholds from whomever He wills, as He extended to Persia and Rome and narrowed it for the Arabs, and He varied among individuals, between those among whom He extended and those upon whom He narrowed. This definitively shows that He has no partner and that He alone is the one who disposes of affairs. Thus He cut off the thoughts of His servants who are granted success from anything other than Him, so that they would turn to Him and devote themselves to Him, for His worship is truly the keys [to all things]. ﴿Ask forgiveness of your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving﴾ [Nuh: 10], ﴿He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain﴾ [Nuh: 11], ﴿and provide you with wealth and children﴾ [Nuh: 12].

﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Talaq: 11]. (p-٢٦٣) ﴿And if the people of the cities had believed and been righteous, We would have opened to them blessings from the heaven and the earth﴾ [al-A'raf: 96]. ﴿And if the People of the Scripture had believed and been righteous, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to gardens of bliss﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 65]. ﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 66].

Since it was as if it were said: "Why did He do that?", He gave the reason in His saying, emphasizing it, because the deeds of most people in acts of disobedience are like the deeds of one who thinks that He, glorified is He, is unaware of their deeds: ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of all things﴾. Therefore no act of His occurs except that it proceeds according to the most perfect of the laws of wisdom. Had He extended provision to the Arabs and their strength and then granted them the dominion of the people of Persia and Rome, they would not have been able to sustain it with their power, and He would not have enabled them. And in everything, small or great, of wisdom, there is something whose subtle aspects the most excellent of nations cannot grasp.

When it was established that all things belong to Him and that none other than Him has any power to dispose of existence, this led to the conclusion that no one other than Him can lay down the paths of the religions, which are the greatest of provisions and the greatest distributor of provisions. So He informed them that He has not prescribed any religion, ancient or recent, other than that upon which they agreed at times of hardship. He said, indicating what He concluded the previous verse with, namely the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, and encouraging adherence to what He guided to and indicated: ﴿He has prescribed for you﴾, meaning He laid down and established a clear, manifest, and evident path, ﴿O community, the final one,﴾ ﴿among the religion﴾ from among the paths (p-264) that are manifest and straight, and religion is that by which one acts and is recompensed. Since the context concerned religion, and they were the ones addressed in this context with the command to follow it, because the Lawgiver had brought it to them, and since they, through their imitation of their fathers, regarded whatever was older as greater and wiser, He mentioned to them the first of the prophets sent to those who opposed them, and said: ﴿That which He enjoined﴾, that is, with a great enjoining after informing them that He had legislated it, ﴿upon Noah﴾, in the most ancient time, as He concluded it through the tongue of the Seal (of the Prophets), and sent with it those who came between them of the famous prophets, because nothing other than it pleases Him. So if you are only averse to entering this religion because of its recency, then it is the oldest of the religions, and everything else is recent. Moreover, He did not send any prophet from among your prophets or from others except with it, and the primordial natures have always unanimously testified to it, and so have the later natures, even the most obstinate hearts, at times of hardship, forever. So enter into it with insight.

Since the miraculous character is specific to us, He brought it forth in the mode of majesty, expressing it by revelation, and by the origin of the connecting things, and indicating the increase of its greatness by placing it before those who came before him, while arranging them when mentioned according to their order of existence. So He said: ﴿And that which We revealed to you﴾. He used the singular pronoun as an added magnification of His greatness, indicating (p-265) that no one grasps its true understanding except him, ﷺ. He also indicated the greatness of what was given to Ibrahim and his descendants through what appeared of its effects, in the mode of majesty, and its deficiency compared with what came to our Prophet, ﷺ, by the expression "enjoined." So He said: ﴿And We enjoined﴾, that is, according to the dazzling majesty that We possess and through which those miracles appeared, ﴿upon Ibrahim﴾, the one whom We saved from the plot of Namrud by fire and otherwise, and whom We granted, in his old age, Isma'il and Ishaq. He is the greatest ancestor of the Arabs, and they are called, most of all, by the title of fathers. So let them act according to what We enjoined upon him. ﴿And Musa﴾, to whom We sent down the Torah as an admonition and a detailed explanation of everything. ﴿And Isa﴾, to whom We sent down the Gospel, in which there is guidance, light, and admonition, and We stored up for him in Our heaven the law of the Seal, the Conqueror.

When the listener's longing for what was revealed and enjoined became intense, He brought it forth in the form of a command, saying, substituting for the object of "shara'a" or beginning a new sentence: ﴿That establish﴾, that is, O you who are legislated for from this final community and from the past nations, ﴿the religion﴾, that is, that upon which the creatures agreed through returning to what they were naturally created upon at times of necessity, which is monotheism, and describing Him with all attributes of perfection absolutely, and other than that of everything with which He sent His messengers. This is on the assumption that "an" is a verbal particle (masdariyyah). It is also permissible that it be an explanatory particle (mufassirah), because of the prior presence of something having the meaning of speech. (p-266) When He magnified it by commanding gathering, He followed it with magnification through prohibiting division, saying: ﴿And do not be divided﴾, that is, a great division, as indicated by the affirmation of the "ta'" (in the verb), and it seems that this is an indication of warning against division in the fundamentals, while permitting independent reasoning in the branches according to one's capacity. ﴿Therein﴾, that is, in the religion, at times of ease, when one turns among its pleasant things which the Lawgiver has bestowed, the one who commands it and encourages following it and warns against abandoning it. And unite upon what was sent by Him to whom you ascribed all attributes of perfection at times of hardship, without any disagreement whatsoever about anything. For division is the cause of destruction, and gathering is the cause of salvation. So be one hand, O People of the Book. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allah﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 64].

When He forbade division, He urged adherence to the unity that is necessary for it, by giving as the reason for the prohibition His saying: ﴿It is hard upon the polytheists﴾, that is, it is great, grievous, and burdensome, to the point that their breasts are constricted by it, namely ﴿that to which you call them﴾, O Prophet, the Conqueror, the Seal, of unity forever upon what they agreed upon at times of necessity, concerning the oneness of the One, the Subduer. So because of its burden upon them, they strive to divide you from it. For if you divide from it (p-267) you would have followed the envious enemy and opposed the loving friend. Since the report of its burden upon them might give the impression that their followers follow them in it, He removed that impression by His saying in answer to one who seems to have said: "How is there any way, in light of that, for anyone to enter this religion?", turning away from the mode of majesty to something greater, to magnify the power over all hearts: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses the comprehensive attributes of majesty and the execution of command. ﴿Chooses﴾, that is, selects with utmost care and directs ﴿to Him﴾, that is, to this religion to which you call them, ﴿whom He wills﴾ for His choosing.

When He, glorified be He, mentioned this purpose without any striving on the part of the one chosen, He followed it with the additional meaning of guidance by conduct, saying: ﴿And guides to Him﴾ through granting success in obedience ﴿whoever turns back﴾, that is, one who has in himself the capacity to continually renew his return to the levels of His obedience at every moment, inwardly, after returning outwardly to the ranks that He has written for him. It is as if the arrival at them had been a descent from them, and by his advancement through stations, through states of obedience, he returns to them.

[p-268] Since "the polytheists" in this verse refers, along with the worshippers of idols, to the People of the Book, who took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God because they accepted from them the declaring lawful and unlawful (al-tahlil wa-l-tahrim), and since this implied that they had separated from the people of obedience, and it also suggested that they had separated only out of ignorance, He spoke, linking to what is implied by the context: "So the messengers came to the people, established the religion for them, and made its aim fully clear to them. Then God chose some of them and misguided others, and they split apart." Then: ﴿And they did not become divided﴾, that is, the polytheists before you, among the People of the Book and others, regarding their religions, ﴿except﴾, and He introduced the preposition (al-jarr) to indicate that the time was not comprehensive, so He said: ﴿after the knowledge had come to them﴾, that is, through the tongues of their prophets, who did not bring confusion. ﴿The knowledge﴾, that is, of what does not permit division with it. From it is that division is misguidance. The preposition also indicates that the division occurred while knowledge was present, not after a long time had passed, such that forgetfulness of all of that entered their knowledge. This is a demonstration of the great power of God the Exalted in His control over hearts. So beware lest your condition be like theirs, and let your fear of your Lord and your hope in Him be intense.

Since abandoning the path of knowledge is strange and improbable, He spoke, clarifying that what drove them to this was the portions of the souls (huzuz al-anfus), from which there is no escape except through God's protection (ismat Allah): ﴿out of rebellion﴾, that is, their division was out of enmity, with no doubt about it, which is clearly wrongdoing, for the sake of the portions of the souls and the following of desires, from which the servant must keep far by having no will of his own at all, but rather his will following the command of his Master.

[p-269] Since absolute rebellion (al-baghy) contradicts noble moral qualities, and therefore committing it is strange, He increased the wonder at it by explaining that the rebellion did not extend beyond their own community to others, but was specific to them, so He said: ﴿among themselves﴾.

Since this requires treatment, He spoke, linking to what is implied: "So were it not for God's power and His gentleness, they would never have gathered again after the division." ﴿And had it not been for a word﴾, that is, one that has no alteration, ﴿that had preceded﴾, that is, in eternity, by delaying them until their appointed terms. Since their being given respite and the gentleness toward them was mercy to them, He made clear that this is only for the sake of the best of creation, so that they would become his followers and thereby increase in honor. He singled him out with mention, as an indication of this, and said, comforting him (ﷺ) by turning the speech to the attribute of benevolence, to please him with what he hopes for regarding his community. He intensified this by adding it to the pronoun, thus indicating that his benevolence toward them is a benevolence befitting his station and fitting his noble purpose and aim: ﴿from your Lord﴾, that is, the One who has been benevolent to you by making you the best of creation and their leader. The word preceded regarding their being given respite ﴿until a specified term﴾, a term set for their lifetimes and then for their gathering in the Hereafter. ﴿It would have been decided﴾ in the easiest and most facile manner ﴿between them﴾ at the time of the division, by destroying the wrongdoer and saving the one in the right.

Since He has informed about the condition of earlier peoples, and since those among the People of the Book in his time (ﷺ) claimed complete knowledge of it and unanimity upon it, all of which calls to hasten to inherit this final, comprehensive Book, [p-270] and since some of them adopted asceticism, turning away from the world, and other things that imply they were upon insight regarding their affair, and denying that they had any kind of doubt, He spoke in a manner that encompasses others as well, emphasizing this as an alert: ﴿And indeed those who﴾. Since the intended meaning is reaching the Book without any contender, and there is no need to know the one who transmits it, the verb is in the passive: ﴿were made to inherit the Book﴾, that is, the complete, final one. They are this community, since its Book abrogated what came before it, and the others were like one who had died, so they inherited, as He the Exalted said: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants﴾ [Fatir: 32]. Their state, in their empowerment to act upon the Book through memorization and understanding, and the absence of any contender to their claim, was like that of the heir and the one from whom inheritance passes. He said: ﴿after them﴾, that is, those who divided, and He affirmed the preposition since the time was not comprehensive: ﴿are in doubt about it﴾, that is, about the inheritance of the Book, which calls for unity and not division, because of the good it contains. This is because of their acting as doubters do, so they say: it is sorcery, poetry, soothsaying, or the like, and that the one who brought it is not truthful, after their having become aware of the miracles he brought and after knowing him. As for the Arabs and those who dwelt among them of the People of the Book, it is by its inimitability, together with the good tidings of him contained in the books of the People of the Book; [p-271] and as for those who did not dwell among them, it is by the call of their own Book. ﴿Disquieting﴾, that is, causing one to fall into suspicion, which causes one to fall into need, which causes one to fall into the vicissitudes of time, which are its calamities, afflictions and misfortunes. This is on the understanding that the intended Book is ours. It is also possible that the pronoun refers specifically to the People of the Book, and the Book is their own Book, and their doubt about it is their acting contrary to what it called them to, namely following our Book by following our Prophet (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 15:

When their deviation from the commands of the Book that came from God was established by this, the command to him ﷺ to convey to the people what benefits them, concerning the message of his Lord who sent down those Books in a single verse, detailed in ten words, each word of which contains a ruling in itself, was made its consequence. They said: there is no parallel to it except the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi), for it consists of ten principles, each principle being independent in itself. He said, making the result of their state the striving to remove it and to act contrary to it: ﴿So for that﴾, i.e., for this exalted revelation whose objectives He enjoined upon all the Messengers, the possessors of great laws among the steadfast messengers (ulu al-'azm) and others, or for that distortion which distances from what is right (p-272) and creates doubt about the matter of the Book.

Since the context of the call to creation was to what He revealed to him and sent down to him, He placed first His saying: ﴿call﴾ to that to which God has sent you, namely the agreement upon what God commanded: gathering upon the upright religion (al-millah al-hanifiyyah). Since the one who calls others does not benefit their call unless he benefits himself, He said: ﴿and be steadfast﴾, i.e., seek from your Lord the strength to bear the hardships of the call so that He may help you in it, and make him (the one who calls) fulfill what he calls to and what is obligatory upon him ﴿as you have been commanded﴾ by One who has no commander over Him, in the details of the call: with gentleness, with firmness, with moderation, and other matters, including speaking to people in what their minds can bear and training them according to what benefits them.

Since everything that opposes Our Book is desire, and everything that opposes Our Book is mere desire, He said: ﴿and do not follow﴾, i.e., deliberately, ﴿their desires﴾ in anything whatsoever, for desire calls to no good, and what is intended from each person is that he do what he was commanded for the sake of the fact that he was commanded, not for the sake of his desire for it.

Since they had split apart over the Book, doubting, believing in some of it and disbelieving in some of it, He commanded him with what contradicts their state, so He said: ﴿And say﴾, i.e., to all the sects and to everyone to whom speech is possible, for you have been sent to all creation: ﴿I believe in what﴾ (p-273) i.e., in everything. Since the most complete of people in faith are those most mindful of the attributes of perfection, of majesty and beauty, He turned the speech to the Greatest Name, indicating the taking of the highest paths in this, so He said: ﴿God has sent down﴾, i.e., He to whom belongs complete greatness, ﴿of a Book﴾; I do not differentiate between any of His Books nor any of His Messengers. Rather, every Book whose descent upon a Messenger has been established, whose messengership has been confirmed by a miracle, I believe in it and call to it, as the perfection of the theoretical faculty requires. Abu 'Ali al-Qali said in Dhayl al-Amali: Abu Bakr — he is Ibn al-Anbari — related to us; Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Uthman related to us; Sihab ibn al-Harith related to us; Bishr ibn 'Imarah informed us from Muhammad ibn Suqah who said: A man came to 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what is faith, or how is faith? He said: Faith rests on four pillars: on patience, certainty, justice and jihad. Patience has four branches: longing, compassion, asceticism and vigilance. Whoever longs for Paradise turns away from desires; whoever fears the Fire refrains from what is forbidden; whoever is ascetic in this world takes misfortunes lightly; whoever awaits death hastens to good deeds. Certainty has four paths: insight of discernment, interpretation of wisdom, admonition of lesson and the way of the earlier ones. Whoever perceives discernment interprets wisdom; whoever interprets wisdom knows the lesson; whoever knows the lesson knows the way; whoever knows the way is as if he were among the earlier ones. (p-274) Justice has four branches: deep understanding, the blossom of forbearance, the garden of knowledge, and the laws of judgment. Whoever understands gathers knowledge; whoever is forbearing does not go astray in judgment; whoever knows recognizes the laws of judgment; whoever is forbearing does not neglect his affair and lives among people. Jihad has four branches: enjoining good, forbidding evil, truthfulness in critical moments, and hatred of the corrupt. Whoever enjoins good strengthens the backs of the believers; whoever forbids evil humbles the noses of the corrupt; whoever is truthful in critical moments has fulfilled what is upon him; whoever hates the hypocrites is angry for God's sake and God is angry for his sake, so He brings him near and raises his station. He said: The man stood up and kissed his head.

Since he informed about justice in the theoretical faculty, he followed that with it in the practical faculty, so He said: ﴿And I have been commanded﴾, i.e., by the One who has all command, to do what He commanded me of what He sent down to me, ﴿to act justly﴾, i.e., in order that I act justly ﴿among you﴾, O you who are divided in religions, among Arabs and non-Arabs, among jinn and humans, as the perfection of the practical faculty calls to. Then He gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿God﴾, i.e., He to whom belongs all dominion (p-275) ﴿is our Lord and your Lord﴾, i.e., our Creator and the one who manages all our affairs; therefore He commanded us to act justly in a general manner, because all are His servants.

Since the Lord is one, He produced from this His saying: ﴿For us are our deeds﴾, specifically belonging to us, you do not extend us to other than ourselves, ﴿and for you are your deeds﴾, specifically belonging to you, they do not extend you to other than yourselves, because there is no reason for us to take the deed of one of us and give it to another, for that is done only by one with a purpose, while He, glorified be He, encompasses all attributes of perfection, so He is exalted above purposes.
