When he reached, by completing this sentence in removing doubt and establishing the truth, that which is like the sun, due to the establishment of the messengership through miracles, the inimitability of this Book, and its agreement with what is with the People of the Book, and the clarification of these two premises about which no one among creation disputes, the result of that was: ﴿There is no argument﴾, i.e., existing through arguing by one of us against the other, ﴿between us and you﴾, because the matter has reached complete manifestation, so there is no further benefit in argument, and nothing remains except disputing with swords and circulating the cups of death, for we know, by God's informing us in His Book, which His inimitability has shown to all creatures, that it is His speech, (p-276) so we hear it from Him for that reason: that we are upon pure truth and that you are upon pure falsehood. We have given you an excuse and brought you through its proofs to direct witnessing, so nothing remains except the sword, in acting upon the virtue of courage.

Since this is the place where it might be said: Do you not fear God regarding those you fight, who are His servants, he answered with his saying, manifesting rather than concealing, to magnify the matter: ﴿God﴾, i.e., He who is the Most Wise of judges, ﴿will gather us together﴾, i.e., us and you upon one religion, if He wills, so there would be no fighting; and in the Hereafter, in every case, He will judge between us. ﴿And those who have wronged will know what a return they will be returned to﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 227]. So we did not undertake fighting except with insight.

Since the one who gathers people together may have an outcome other than that, he clarified that the matter concerning it is other than that, so he said, conjoining it to what its estimate is: from Him was the beginning: ﴿And to Him﴾, i.e., not to other than Him, from the standpoint of this name which gathers all attributes, ﴿is the final return﴾, sensibly and in meaning, due to the completeness of His might, the comprehensiveness of His greatness and the perfection of His mercy. As for what was between the beginning and the return of matters which seem to be outside (p-277) the control of another, they were only a trial from Him by which He establishes proof against the servants according to what they know among themselves; and whoever had control over them other than Him, their action was only a sudden matter which makes the proof valid against them and obligates them with the proof.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 16:

Since the sense is: those who responded to Him willingly in this world after this clarification and manifestation, and abandoned disputation, their proof remaining firm, and theirs are good pleasure and lasting bliss, He followed it with His words, beginning with the relative pronoun so as to connect it with what conveys renewal and continuity: ﴿And those who dispute﴾, that is, they put forward, against His true religion, doubts from dubious claims that they call proofs. Perhaps the idgham (assimilation of consonants, a grammatical process) indicates that the people of this kind are hypocrites who cast their doubts in secrecy, so the hearts of their likes absorb them and they become desires, and their matter weakens. This is supported by restricting the futility (duhud) to what is with the Lord. ﴿in Allah﴾, that is, in the religion of the Supreme King, so that they may return people, after they have entered the light of guidance, to the darkness of misguidance.

Since establishing proof and manifesting a miracle is an obligation binding on everyone who has received it, with the matter reaching a degree of clarity such that disputation falls away with it, He said, informing that what is in the state of potential existence may rightly be described as existing, and alerting by the prepositional phrase to the blameworthiness of this disputation, even if its duration is brief: ﴿after what﴾. And since the intended meaning is the bare fact of response, not response from a specific respondent, He said: ﴿has been responded to﴾, that is, the Messenger (ﷺ) responded to it. All people, by what becomes clear to them, become responders in potential, even if they have not responded in act, for the matter has become manifest to the utmost degree, and nothing remains but obstinacy. This sentence is the meaning and the fruit of His saying ﴿There is no argument between us and you﴾ [al-Shura: 15].

Since whoever's outward contradicts his inward is weak in argument, flimsy in texture, He expressed with a second subject, singular for the argument, indicating its weakness: ﴿their argument﴾, that is, which they claimed to be an argument. He predicated of this second subject, so that it and its predicate together would be a predicate of the first, and said: ﴿is futile﴾, that is, slippery, so it is gone and not firm, because it stands in opposition to what is manifest like the sun, rather, clearer. The expression (…) draws attention to the attribute of beneficence and nearness, indicating the intensity of the manifestness of the futility in their argument, because ʿinda (with, at) is used for matters that are manifest and familiar. The attribute of lordship (tarbiyah) connotes tenderness and kindness, and the addition to their pronoun requires further gentleness and compassion. So it indicates that it is scattered dust at the closest scrutiny, especially when He is described with might, dominance and wrath. The meaning is that its futility is very evident, even if they are treated with beneficence, and even if they are singled out with extra kindness and goodness. How does this compare with what would be said, "in the presence of One All-Knowing, All-Powerful," for that understands that its futility is not perceived except by one of perfect knowledge and complete power, and yet it is strange? Thus there is in it a kind of praise of their argument in general: ﴿with their Lord﴾, that is, the One who has been good to them by bestowing the intellect, by which He made them in the best of forms. So whenever they strip it of desire, it guides them to the fact that all they were in is falsehood. In this is an indication that the least of what He punishes them with is the cutting off of His beneficence from them, and that the falsehood of what they called an argument becomes evident to every intelligent person, which brings them disgrace in this world and punishment in the Hereafter. Moreover, the cutting off of His beneficence is, upon reflection, the highest of punishments. ﴿And upon them﴾, in addition to the cutting off of beneficence, ﴿is wrath﴾, that is, a punishment befitting their blameworthy state and their reprehensible attribute, and from it is expulsion. So they are expelled from His door, distanced from His presence, and humiliated by His veil. Since the expression with ʿala (upon) conveyed that they were blamed by the superiority of vengeance over them, the expression with lam (for) was not unsuitable. Rather, it conveyed mockery and reproach, so He said: ﴿And for them﴾, that is, despite that, ﴿is a severe punishment﴾, whose true description you cannot reach. The verse alludes to prevailing over the apostates and striking them with all severity, because of the evil of their station with Him, as the situation revealed when al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) called them to fight, and Allah be well pleased with him.

The Almighty, after He had decreed what He threatened them with, having ruled that their arguments were refuted (*duḥūḍ*), and since none decrees a matter with certainty except one whose command is effective and whose judgment is all-encompassing, He drew attention to this, explaining what by which one knows the firmness of proofs and their refutation. That refutation entails wrath from Allah, which leads to punishment. He stated this with the words, turning the speech to the Greatest Name (*al-Ism al-A'ẓam*, the Greatest Name of God) to indicate the greatness of the One who gives this report: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom belongs all sovereignty, ﴿who﴾. By using the expression "sending down," He indicated that what is meant is the whole Book, in which there is no flaw in any part of it. So He said: ﴿sent down the Book﴾, that is, brought about its sending down, He alone and no other, ﴿with truth﴾, that is, clothed in the most perfect manner (p-٢٨١) with the established matter that is not altered, and by means of the true action, general to statements, deeds and beliefs, so that you may distinguish the established proofs from others.

Since the Book commands justice in word and in deed, and since among the perceptible aspects of its commands is measuring by precise measures, He specified and expressed it with the most upright of them, indicating that the Book is more just in justice to the intellect and clearer than the balance is to the senses. He said: ﴿and the Balance﴾, that is, the command concerning it, intending by it its very reality and all of its kinds; rather, all justice mentioned in "there is no justice between you" is meant figuratively. Since it has been established that whoever disputes concerning it, his argument will be refuted when he is called to account on the Hour, and so he will be punished, and since the context points to the implicit meaning as a consolation for him (ﷺ) concerning what he suffers in carrying out what he was commanded of justice in all his words and deeds, and in his patience with their harm: whoever turns to the Book for meanings and to the Balance for concrete things, and builds his affair on the realization of justice in both, through both, will succeed; and whoever neglects that will fail, his argument will be refuted and will fall at a fourth of its station. And what will make you know? Perhaps someone who hastens in this world to be seized, because his appointed term, which the Word had preceded in delaying, has drawn near. He joined to it his saying, addressing the speech to the highest of creation, to magnify the matter: ﴿And what will make you know﴾ (p-٢٨٢) O most perfect of creation, ﴿that the Hour﴾, which was pointed to in this verse by His saying ﴿with their Lord﴾ [al-Shūrā: 16], after He had stated it explicitly in other verses, ﴿is near?﴾.

Since the feminine form of *al-sā'ah* (the Hour) is not true feminine, because it means "the time," He mentioned it as masculine, saying ﴿qarīb﴾ (near). This conveys that it is possessed of severities, that its severities are masculine severities, and that its nearness is swifter than the flash of lightning because of its firmness in truth. Or He mentioned it masculine by intending the cause, that is, possessing nearness; or by omitting a modifier, that is, its coming. In every case it indicates its magnification, that is, you are in a position of nearness to the Resurrection, so that what they were threatened with will befall them, that which should be feared. Thus justice will appear in it by the balances of equity for all deeds, an appearance about which no one will dispute, so that whoever fulfilled [his duty] will be honored, and whoever transgressed and was harsh will be disgraced.

Al-Biqa'i, *Nazm al-Durar*, on Surah 42, verse 18:

When he (Allah) conveyed its nearness by expressing it with *la'alla* (perhaps), this indicated that the state of one who seeks its hastening is the state of one who hopes for a beloved thing, and this is a great ignorance on his part. He then began to distinguish people with regard to it, saying, indicating that the sensible person should prepare for it so as to be saved when it comes, since its signs are manifest, without investigating whether it is near or far, ﴿those who seek to hasten it﴾ (p-283) — i.e., they seek that it come before its appointed time — ﴿but those who do not believe in it﴾, i.e., this does not occur to them at all, and they are not apprehensive of it, and they think it is falsehood. The situation would have required that they be the most averse of people to it, but what drove them to this was their denial of it, their mockery, and their assumption that it will not happen, which is ignorance on the part of those who acknowledge His power, exaltedness, and greatness.

When he indicated the ignorance of the disbelievers, he indicated their opposites, saying: ﴿And those who believe﴾ — even if they are at the first stages of faith — ﴿are apprehensive﴾, i.e., fearful with great fear, ﴿of it﴾, because Allah guided them through their faith, so their breasts became mines of knowledge and their hearts became springs of lights. They were certain of the great terrors within it, so they feared, out of their refinement, that they might, despite their righteousness, be among the people of the Fire. When he put apprehension first, as a reminder that the sensible person should fear what may possibly occur, he said: ﴿and they know that it is the truth﴾, informing that they have insight into its matter, so they do not seek to hasten it. Thus the verse is an instance of *ihtibak* (a rhetorical device in which one term is mentioned and its opposite omitted, and vice versa): he mentioned hastening first as an indication of the omission of its opposite second, and apprehension second as an indication of the omission of its opposite first.

Ibn Kathir said: It has been related through channels that reach the level of *tawatur* (mass transmission, a hadith reported by so many routes that its authenticity is beyond doubt) in the *Sahih* collections, the *Hasan* collections, the *Sunan* and the *Masanid* (collections): "A man asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in a loud voice, while he was on some of his journeys, and called out: 'O Muhammad!' The Prophet (ﷺ) answered him with a voice like his: 'Ha'um' (come here). He said: 'When is the Hour?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'Woe to you! It is coming. What have you prepared for it?' He said: 'The love of Allah and His Messenger.' He said: 'You are with whom you love.'"

Ibn Kathir said: His saying in the hadith, "A person is with whom he loves," is undoubtedly mutawatir. The point is that he did not answer him about the time of the Hour, but rather commanded him to prepare for it. (End of Ibn Kathir's words.) This is conditional upon disavowal of the enemies of Allah, as shown by the story of Abu Talib, for the love of the friend did not benefit him fully without disavowal of the enemy.

When, by the definition of the Truth, he informed that it is established with complete permanence, with no end to it at all and no cessation of its effects, he produced his saying, emphatically and with reverence, in opposition to their denial: ﴿Unquestionably, those who dispute﴾, i.e., who display their doubt in a manner of intense obstinacy, seeking to make the doubt of others manifest, from *mariytu al-naqata* (I milked the she-camel), when one rubs her udder vigorously for milking in order to extract whatever milk may be in it, ﴿concerning the Hour﴾, i.e., the Resurrection and what it contains, ﴿are indeed in far-off error﴾ (p-285), i.e., in a path of deviation far from the truth, ﴿very far﴾ from the correct course. For it has, from the manifest proofs in reason, supported by definitive transmission, what places it, during its absence, as if it were among sensible things; were the veil to be lifted, I would not increase in certainty.

When the outcome for the two groups was that the disbelievers displayed fear while in the utmost security, and the believers concealed their security while in the most distressing fear, and this itself is subtle kindness (lutf), since it is reaching a thing through its opposite, and the term also denotes conveying benefit to creation in a manner whose perception is subtle, and since what most delays a person in matters of religion is his preoccupation with provision, this produced His saying: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom the whole affair belongs, so He does what He wills, ﴿is Subtle (Latif)﴾, that is, He is profound in the world and in bestowing goodness by conveying benefits and averting harms in a manner whose perception is refined. Al-Qushayri said: al-Latif is the One who knows the fine details and hidden subtleties of affairs, and al-Mulattif is the One who is gracious and benevolent. Both are true of His attributes, glorified is He, and the term lutf is used most often in describing Him with benevolence in religious matters. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': it is a compound name made up of knowledge, mercy, and hidden gentleness, ﴿to His servants﴾, and that is the end of the quotation.

As for the believer, it is clear. As for the disbeliever, the least of His kindness to him is that He does not hasten to punish him in this world, and does not chastise him beyond what he deserves in the Hereafter. Thus the first name is a warning (takhwif), and the second is an apparent hope whose inner meaning is a warning, indicating what ought to be the balance of fear and hope, with fear being the predominant one.

Since this attribute is most manifest in provision, He widens it for one who has no means, and withholds it from one who is in the utmost of strength and power, raises the weak coward and lowers the strong brave. All of this is according to what He knows of their inner states and what He adds to their deeds. He said, indicating this as a resumption (istinaf) for one who asks about the manner of the subtle kindness: ﴿He provides for whom He wills﴾, whenever He wills, in a manner of abundance, or constriction, or moderation, with nothing preventing Him from any of that. He withholds provision from whom He wills when He knows the term of his life has run out, so He takes him to Himself. So strive with your souls in seeking His good pleasure, and do not turn your attention to fear of need, for He has already decreed provision and has forbidden excessive pursuit of it.

Since no one other than Him is able to do this, owing to what it requires of perfect strength and all-encompassing might, He said: ﴿And He is the Strong (al-Qawi)﴾, that is, (p-٢٨٧) His giving is never constrained by anything, ﴿the Mighty (al-Aziz)﴾, so none can prevent Him from anything.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 20:

When he had shown by this that provision lies entirely in His hand, he followed it with what discourages seeking the provision of the body and encourages seeking the provision of the soul, and said, by way of resumption (istic'naf), as an answer to one who asks: does provision come through intense striving or not? He began with the provision of the soul because of its nobility: ﴿Whoever desires﴾, i.e., whether of noble or lowly station, ﴿desires﴾. Since the central aim of the surah is religion, and religion is a transaction between the servant and his Lord, one intends by it what one intends by tilling (harth), namely the attainment of benefit; and since tilling is among the most important causes of gain, and Paradise is "barren plains whose planting is the remembrance of Allah," he expressed general gain by tilling and said: ﴿the tilling of the Hereafter﴾, i.e., its deeds by which benefits are gathered. Since the causes of tillings and their fruits cannot be withheld or made to succeed except by Allah, and since the human being imagines he has power in this matter, He, glorified is He, alerted by shifting to the style of majesty that His command in this matter cannot be resisted, repelled, or contested: ﴿We increase for him﴾, i.e., by Our majesty which no one can alter, ﴿in his tilling﴾, by helping him in righteous deeds through illuminating the heart, purifying the state, calming the inner self, and penetrating insight into what harms and benefits, and multiplying its reward for him, from tenfold for every good deed up to an endless measure, and covering for him from the world what We have decreed for him, as help for him in what he has turned to of (p-288) the Hereafter. He omitted mention of the world in this half as an alert that it is too base to be mentioned, though it is known from other verses.

﴿And whoever desires﴾, i.e., whether strong or weak, ﴿the tilling of this world﴾, i.e., its provisions which are sought through toil and striving, and he takes satisfaction in it, content with it, preferring it over the Hereafter, ﴿We give him of it﴾ what We have apportioned to him. Even if he is careless about it and does not seek it, it would still come to him; and not everyone attains all he wishes even if he strives with all his effort. As for the Hereafter, whatever its seeker intends of its deeds is obtained for him even if he does not perform them. ﴿And he has no share in the Hereafter﴾, i.e., while the seeker of this world has no share in the Hereafter at all. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"Give glad tidings to this community of brightness, elevation, victory, and establishment in the earth. Whoever among them performs deeds of the Hereafter for the sake of this world will have no share in the Hereafter." Narrated by Ahmad, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, al-Hakim, who said: its chain is sound, and al-Bayhaqi. That is because deeds are by intentions, and every person has only what he intended. This is a neglect of them, so he has not intended them, while they are too noble to be granted to one who turns away from them (p-289) and they remain far from one who turns toward them until they destroy him in their pitfalls; whereas the Hereafter turns toward one who turns toward it many times over, and calls out to one who turns away from it to desist from his error and misguidance. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': the people of intention are of kinds: one who wants this world, one who wants the Hereafter, and one who wants the Truth, exalted and most high. The sign of wanting this world is that one is pleased with increasing his worldly wealth at the cost of his religion, and turns away from the poor Muslims, and that his needs in supplication are confined to this world; the sign of wanting the Hereafter is the opposite of that. As for the sign of wanting Allah, glorified and exalted, as He said, "They desire His Face," it is casting off both worlds, and freedom from the creation, and deliverance from the hand of the self. End of quote. Its summary is that one should devote his times to fulfilling the rights of the Truth and the rights of creation and purifying the self, not out of greed for Paradise nor fear of Fire, but in compliance with the command of the Sovereign King, besides whom there is no god, because He is worthy of that, while acknowledging that one will never truly measure Allah with His due measure.

(p-290) When there had been established what He has legislated of the religion, which He enjoined upon all the prophets, so that its foundations became clear, its branches and details became manifest, its wonders appeared, and its jewels and signs shone forth, and He concluded with the supreme law concerning the affairs of both abodes, which is observed and which no one else is able to bring about, the meaning becomes evident without concealment: "This is the Sharia of God, which He has approved for His servants, and He has judged that devotion to it is not harmful to the pursuit of provision, and He has decreed the provisions, so no one has the power to add anything to his provision or to diminish anything from it. Will they accept it?" He balances this with His words, exalted is He, affirming, rebuking, and alerting to what is the root of straying from His firmly established laws and His settled and fixed legislations: ﴿Or do they have partners?﴾, that is, these people who swerve right and left, ﴿partners﴾ according to their claim, who have shared with the Legislator whose might has already been explained and whose majesty and greatness in His command have become manifest, to the extent that ﴿they have legislated﴾, that is, the partners who have taken up and pursued a path, ﴿for them﴾, that is, for the disbelievers. It is also possible that the meaning is: the disbelievers legislated for their partners ﴿of the religion﴾ in acts of worship and customs, which establish in minds that there must be a recompense for them, due to what their customs have run upon, without accountability from those under their control, and they decreed for them from the provisions. He turned away from the style of greatness to the Greatest Name, indicating that with greatness there is (p-291) of honor, of which forbearance is a part, which requires that they not be hastily seized. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿that which God has not permitted﴾, that is, which God enables the servants to do by commanding them to it and approving it, the King with whom no one has any command. His attributes have erased every attribute, and before them every greatness has shrunk; yet they turned to Him alone, not to others, because He is the one counted upon. If that is so, then let them make happy whoever turns to this world, which is the target of their concern, so they know no other, by giving him all his desire; and let them make wretched whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its striving. He attributed the legislation to the idols because they are its cause, just as they were the cause of misguidance, in His words, exalted and high, recounting from Abraham, His friend, upon him be peace: ﴿My Lord, they have led many of the people astray﴾ [Ibrahim: 36]. And partners are attributed to them at times because they are the ones who take them, and at times to God, exalted is He, because they associated them with Him. The expression comes according to the context.

When He knew with certainty that the meaning is: "Were it not that these acts which they perform without permission from Him do not diminish His dominion, exalted is He, in anything, and do not harm anyone except their doer, although they are by His will, then were He to prevent them from them they would not reach anything of them," He followed it with His words, exalted is He: ﴿And had it not been for the word of decision﴾, which had preceded from eternity, that it would not be (p-292) And since their matter was minor, the verb was put in the passive, so He said: ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾, that is, between those who obeyed His command and adhered to His law, and between those who followed what they had legislated for those they named as partners, in the nearest time. But the decree had already preceded from the pre-eternal eternity, with the measures of things and their determination according to the aspects of wisdom. So they run according to what has been set for them, with no advancing of anything of them, no delay, no change, and no alteration. The matters will be revealed to you, and the hidden things of what has been decreed will become manifest. The separation will occur only in the Hereafter, as the decree has preceded that the just will have an enduring bliss.

Since they were denying that punishment would befall them, He said, emphasizing, as a continuation of what I have supposed, with what the context guides to: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers﴾, by legislating what God has not permitted, of polytheism and other things, ﴿for them is a painful punishment﴾, that is, painful, its affliction being intense.

(p. 293) When it became known from this context, as you see, that a separation is necessary, and that this separation can only take place on the Day of Resurrection, He said, explaining the separation between the two groups on that Day, addressing the most exalted of creation, to indicate that this is not fully understood or known with complete certainty by anyone other than him (ﷺ). Or the intended addressee is everyone who can be addressed, indicating that the matter is so clear that it is not restricted to one person over another. So He said: ﴿You will see﴾, that is, on that Day no sensible person will doubt it, because of the primary innate, rational and transmitted proofs it contains, ﴿the wrongdoers﴾, that is, those who place things other than in their proper places, ﴿fearful﴾, that is, afraid with the greatest fear, as is the state of one who is being called to account by someone above him while he has fallen short. Since the discussion concerns those whom He described as wrongdoers, a firmly established attribute of theirs, it is known that all their deeds are against them. Therefore He expressed it with the verb of earning in its bare form, saying: ﴿of what they have earned﴾, that is, what they did while believing it to be beneficial to them, since that is the utmost of what could benefit them. ﴿And it﴾, that is, its recompense and its evil consequence, which is of the same kind as it, so that it is as if it were itself, ﴿will certainly befall them﴾, without their fear increasing anything for them except punishment in the depths of the fires. That is the manifest loss. That is what the wrongdoers are warned of. ﴿And those who believe﴾ may be in construction as a conjunct to the object of ﴿you see﴾, and may be a conjunct to the whole sentence, in which case it is a subject (of a new sentence). ﴿And do righteous deeds﴾, which are those that God has permitted, not fearing what they have earned, because they are permitted to do it, and it is forgiven them for whatever they neglected in it. ﴿In the gardens of the Gardens﴾, that is, in this world, through the delights God grants them from the pleasant sayings, deeds, knowledge and states, and in the Hereafter in reality, without cessation. ﴿For them is whatever they wish﴾, that is, forever and ever, this being so because it is in the utmost of preservation and nurturing. Alerting to this kind of preservation, He turned to the attribute of excellence, saying: ﴿with their Lord﴾, that is, the One who did not bring them to this great reward except through the goodness of His nurturing of them and the subtlety of His kindness to them, according to the manner in which He nurtured them.

When He mentioned what they will receive as recompense, He magnified it, saying: ﴿That﴾, that is, this recompense, great in rank and lofty in worth, ﴿is﴾, and nothing else is, ﴿the bounty﴾, that is, which is worthy of being surplus beyond the sufficiency of its possessor, even if he spends lavishly, ﴿the great﴾, which fills all aspects of need, and all that others attained of this worldly trash becomes small in its presence. Thus the verse, as you see, is of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which something mentioned in one part is omitted from the parallel part, and vice versa): He affirmed fear first, as an indication of the omission of security second, and the Gardens second, as an indication of the omission of the Fires first.

(p-295) When he had mentioned their station and their final destination in it, he explained its permanence, further magnifying it. So he said, beginning: ﴿That is﴾, meaning the great matter of the Garden and its bliss, and he gave the predicate of the subject with his words: ﴿that which gives good news﴾, meaning any kind of good news according to the one who reads it lightly, and much good news according to the one who reads it heavily. He added to the good news by the Greatest Name, saying, turning the speech toward Himself: ﴿Allah﴾, meaning the Greatest King and the one returned to, while the returning pronoun, "with it," is omitted (p-295), to exalt what is announced, because the context concerns exalting it through the good news. He placed it with the distal particle and with the relative description "that which." He mentioned the Greatest Name and the expression "servants" with its attribution to His own pronoun, glorified is He, so the omission of the object indicated that the action falls upon them and reaches them directly without an intermediary. Thus it became as if it were mentioned, manifest, and in view. So he said: ﴿His servants﴾. It is known that everyone honors the one whom He has singled out for His servanthood.

When he indicated the attribution through their righteousness, he specified it with his words: ﴿who believe﴾, meaning those who affirm the unseen, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, as a confirmation of their faith, ﴿the righteous deeds﴾. That is the good news that was mentioned earlier, which warns those who disbelieve. Since the custom is that a bearer of good news must have a reward, even if he does not ask, because his good news stands in place of a request, Ka'b ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "When Allah announced His acceptance of our repentance, a rider came racing toward me on a horse, and a runner ran on foot, and he climbed Mount Sal' and called out: 'O Ka'b ibn Malik, rejoice, for Allah has accepted your repentance.' The voice was faster than the horse. When the one whose voice I had heard came to me, I took off my two garments and gave them to him, by Allah, I owned no other garments that day, and I borrowed two garments and wore them..." until the end of his narration. It was as if it were said: "What do you seek in return for this good news?" So he was commanded to answer with his words: ﴿Say﴾, meaning to the one who imagined about you what the custom of announcers is: ﴿I do not ask you﴾, meaning now or in the future time, ﴿for it﴾, meaning for the conveying of good news and warning, ﴿any reward﴾, meaning even if it is small, ﴿except﴾, meaning but I ask you ﴿for affection﴾, meaning great and wide love.

Since they were persistent in maintaining ties of kinship, even when distant, and of lineage, for this reason he said: ﴿among the near of kin﴾, meaning contained within it, such that the kin is the place of affection and its container, so that nothing of your love goes outside it. For by it the matter of the religion is completed and the gathering within it becomes perfect. If you join the kinship between me and you, you will not deny me falsely, nor will you reject what I have brought you of the happiness of both abodes. You will succeed with complete success, and the bond between us will endure until we die and then enter the Garden, so our bond will continue forever. This includes all relatives, and there was no clan of Quraysh except that the Prophet (ﷺ) had a kinship with them. Al-Bukhari narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), and he said: "Except that you join what is between me and you of kinship." Al-Bukhari also narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Except that you harm me regarding my kin" (p-297), meaning that you show them kindness and do good to them.

Ibn Kathir said: al-Suddi said: When 'Ali ibn al-Husayn was brought as a captive and placed on the steps of Damascus, a man from the people of Syria stood up and said: "Praise be to Allah who killed you, uprooted you, and cut off the horn of sedition." 'Ali said to him: "Have you read the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Have you not read: ﴿Say: I ask you no reward for it except affection among the near of kin﴾?" He said: "Indeed, you are they." He said: "Yes."

From al-Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah! When some of Quraysh meet some of them, they greet them with a good face, but when they meet us, they meet us with faces we do not recognize." The Prophet (ﷺ) became extremely angry and said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, faith does not enter the heart of a man until he loves you for the sake of Allah and His Messenger." And from him: that he entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Indeed, we go out and see Quraysh conversing, and when they see us, they fall silent." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry, and sweat appeared between his eyes. Then he said: "By Allah, faith does not enter the heart of a Muslim man until he loves you for the sake of Allah and for my kinship." He expressed the exception in the disjunctive form, which is the munqati' (disjunct exception), with the exceptive particle, to intensify the negation by informing that no reward is excepted at all except this affection, if anyone supposes that it is a reward. It may also be that "except" (illa) means "other than" (ghayr), so it is from the type of the verse:

"There is no fault in them, other than that their swords
have notches from the clashing of battalions."

Whoever has a kinship with any Muslim is responsible for being mindful of Allah regarding that kinship, so he joins its owner with everything within his capacity of what Allah has commanded him of reward or punishment. How much more so the kinship of the Prophet (ﷺ), for he (ﷺ) said, in what al-Tabarani narrated and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya (Hilyat al-Awliya') from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him): "The likeness of the People of my House is like the likeness of the Ark of Noah (peace be upon him): whoever boards it is saved, and whoever stays behind from it is destroyed." And he said, in what he narrated in al-Firdaws (a collection of al-Daylami) from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): "My companions are like the stars in the sky; whichever of them you follow, you will be guided." Al-Isfahani said: "We now, in the sea of obligation, need the sound ship and the shining stars. The ship is love of the Family, and the stars are love of the Companions. So we ask Allah for safety and happiness through their love in this world and the Hereafter." And Allah knows best.

Since the decree was definite, that "whoever commits a sin, upon him is its burden," but it was omitted because the context is one of good news, as the ending of the verse indicates along with what precedes it, he joined to it his words: ﴿And whoever earns﴾, meaning acquires, engages in, works at with diligence, striving, intention, and effort, ﴿a good deed﴾, meaning even if it is small. He turned the speech toward the manifestation of greatness, indicating that none increases in goodness except the great, and that goodness may itself be a cause of the greatness of the doer. So He said: ﴿We increase﴾, beyond Our greatness, ﴿for him in it goodness﴾, in a way that does not fall within imagination. Among the increase is that he will have a reward like the reward of whoever follows him in it until the Day of Resurrection, without diminishing their rewards in any way. This is from the reward of the Messengers for conveying it to the nations, so they are independent of seeking anything else. This applies if they are guided by it. If he calls them and they are not guided, he will have a reward like their rewards had they been guided, for their not being guided is not due to his shortcoming. Rather, Allah decrees and does what He wills.

Since they would say: "We have committed such wrongs that nothing benefits along with them," he said, negating that by way of emphasis, giving the reason, clarifying, and turning the speech to the Greatest Name, that such a thing is not within the power of any other's kingdom in any way: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, meaning the One whom nothing overwhelms, ﴿is Oft-Forgiving﴾ to every sin from which its doer repents, or who is worthy of forgiveness even if he does not repent, if He wills. So let no one turn away from the good deed because of a bad deed he has done.

Since affirming a good deed, let alone increasing it, is valid only with forgiveness, and cannot coexist with reckoning, mentioning that attribute, which is the foundation of increase, conveyed it, meaning the increase, with His words: ﴿Most Appreciative﴾ [al-Shura: 23]. He repays the good deed with multiples of it and overlooks the rest of His rights (p-300).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 24:

When He had established that He sent down the Book with truth, and had indicated this, until He concluded with the negation of purpose in the conveying (of the message), so that certainty was attained regarding the content of the report, it was as if it were said, in denunciation of them and rebuke to them: Have they acted upon what We have alerted them to, of that which they claim they are foremost in, namely the joining of the ties of kinship and devotion to the lofty noble qualities by avoiding evil deeds and committing good deeds, and keeping far from lying, obstinacy and slander? So they believed that it is the truth and that it is a revelation from Allah, by the proof that was established for it? ﴿Or do they say﴾ out of obstinacy: ﴿"He has invented it"﴾, i.e., he deliberately fabricated it, intending to cut it off. He mentioned the Supreme King first, as an alert that there is nothing more heinous than lying against the King of kings, though the object is understood from the word "invention" (iftirā'), so He said: ﴿against Allah﴾, the One who encompasses the attributes of perfection; for Him is the all-comprehensive knowledge of whoever fabricates against Him, and the complete power to punish him, ﴿a lie﴾, when he claimed that this Qur'an is from Him and that He sent him for this religion.

Since the estimate, with certainty, is: they indeed say that, and their saying it is a statement whose falsehood is known, because He challenged them with something of its like, in their assumption that He has a like, in order that they might know the correctness of their claim, yet they did not bring anything. And although they may claim that something prevents them from that, namely that they do not permit lying, they are falsifiers, and no intelligent person doubts (p-301) the falsity of that from them too, because it is not impossible for them to forget what they attribute to Allah. Moreover, if He had asked this of them, it would not have been an excuse, because no one doubts that necessities permit prohibited things, and that one commits the lesser of two harms to ward off the greater of them. So bringing a brief speech by which long strifes are quieted and great evils are cut off is of the utmost goodness, for the matter in it is easy and the affair is slight. Thus that, while they commit something greater than it, namely severing the ties of kinship, dividing the word, killing souls, ruining dwellings and destroying wealth, is a conclusive proof that they only abandon it through incapacity. This is the consequence of their saying, which is their attributing to him the deliberate intention of lying. So Allah, the Exalted, said in reply to them, showing their lie in what they said, by showing what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, possesses of the light of the heart that necessarily results from uprightness of speech: ﴿Then if﴾ — and He made the divine name explicit rather than using a pronoun, to magnify the matter, since sealing cannot be done except by one characterized by all the attributes of perfection absolutely, without being restricted by any qualifier at all — so He said: ﴿Allah wills﴾, i.e., the One who has the encompassing of perfection, ﴿He would seal﴾ — and He followed the previous manner of address to the greatest people of intellect — so He said, expressing it with the particle of elevation: ﴿upon your heart﴾, so that He would prevent it from accepting the spirit of this (p-302) revelation, just as He sealed upon the hearts of your enemies against accepting it. Then you would be equal to them, at that time, in incapacity to bring anything of its like, and you would become, were you to say — and may Allah protect you from what they say — something whose ascription to falsehood is valid, one who would say it only while the proofs stand against its falsehood, just as they too remain exposed, while the proofs against their sayings stand against their falsehood. The original form of the speech would have been: "Do they say that, and that they are liars in it?" — because of the fact that Allah has expanded your breast and illuminated your heart, so you do not say a saying except that the proofs stand for its truth. But He conducted the speech in this way because, along with its being more just, it indicates a conditional linkage with the fabrication upon the sealing of hearts, and that definitively indicates that they are the liars, because of the seal upon their hearts, which necessitates that they say what the proofs stand against its being a lie.

Since the estimate, as the context indicates, is: "But He did not will that; rather He willed to make him receptive to the spirit of revelation, aware of the branches of knowledge, so he pours forth kinds of knowledge and calls out to receive marvels of subtleties, and Allah establishes all of that without any (p-303) hindrance or diverter" — He followed it with His saying: ﴿And Allah erases﴾, i.e., the One who has all the attributes of perfection, ﴿the falsehood﴾, which is their saying "he has invented it", and every lie, so He leaves no trace of it. There the loss of the denier appears, and the tongue of the stubborn opponent is cut off. The instrument of erasure is not mentioned, such as words or other things, as a belittling of it, with an indication that He sometimes erases it by Himself without any cause, sometimes by the weakest of causes, and sometimes by something higher than it. Its waw was omitted in writing in all the codices, although it is a resumptive (istinaf) not part of the apodosis, because He, exalted is He, erases falsehood absolutely, as an allusion that He, glorified is He, annihilates its elevation, its height and its dominance, which the waw indicates, matching between its writing and its pronunciation; and its meaning, as an emphasis on the good news: He erases it with an erasure that leaves for it neither trace nor effect, for whoever is seized by His might. And He is patient as He was commanded, for His arrangement, relying on the true promise of Allah, in faith in the unseen and trust in the Messengers, peace and blessings be upon them. In the omission there is also a resemblance to the imperative verb, as an allusion that carrying out this erasure is a matter which must be done in the most complete, most firm, highest and most perfect manner, just as the commanded thing comes from an obeyed king. As for the truth, it is firm, heavy and redoubled, so He said: ﴿And establishes﴾, i.e., He makes it firm in a way that its removal is not possible, ﴿the truth﴾, i.e., each of whose nature is steadfastness (p-304), because He has permitted it and confirmed it. The truth and its establishment are magnified by mentioning the instrument of the act, so He said: ﴿by His words﴾, i.e., those of which ﴿if the sea were ink﴾ [al-Kahf: 109] is the verse, the expression of which that which came to them they claim is fabrication of a lie. The conclusion is that He, glorified is He, established the purity of his intellect, the luminosity of his heart, the soundness of his speech and the rightness of his affair, and the darkness of their hearts and the invalidity of their sayings, an establishment accompanied by its proof: for people of insight, by their incapacity to oppose it; and for the dull, by the establishment of His word and the erasure of their word.

Since they knew that he was upon the truth and they upon falsehood, and whoever's knowledge encompasses a thing is able to do what he wills concerning that thing, He explained this by His saying, giving a reason in the manner of emphasis, because their action was the action of one who supposes that Allah does not know their scheming: ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing﴾, i.e., reaching ﴿of what is within the breasts﴾, i.e., what is in them of what its possessor knows and of what he does not know, so He nullifies their falsehood and establishes His truth, even if the creatures dislike that. ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time﴾ [Sad: 88]. Allah has indeed spoken truly: by the blessing of this Qur'an He established everything that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was saying, and by the sword of (p-305) this proof He nullified everything that they were opposing him in. And who is more truthful in statement than Allah?

When He had informed them of their misguidance and decisively declared their deeds void, He, out of His mercy toward them, encouraged them to repent (tawbah, "repentance"), which is among the truths He establishes, even in its least form: that they utter it with their tongues so that it reaches Him from them. For verbal speech is likely to enter [the heart] only sometimes, and not others, [but it is] perpetually and always. ﴿He who accepts repentance﴾ whenever He wills, reaching it [fully], or passing over it ﴿from His servants﴾ who are sincere in obeying Him. Abu al-Hasan al-Bushanji was asked about repentance and said: "When you remember a sin and find no sweetness in your heart for it."

Since acceptance may occur in the future while still taking account of what has passed, He said: ﴿and pardons the evil deeds﴾, meaning those from which repentance was made, whether small (p-306) or great, and others, so that He does not hold them to account for them if He wills, because repentance erases what came before it, just as Islam, which is a specific kind of repentance, erases what was before it.

Since the transitive use of "accept" with "from" (ʿan) implies that it reaches Him through an intermediary, which might suggest a deficiency in knowledge, He informed of what necessitates His transcendence above that, as encouragement and warning, by His saying: ﴿and He knows﴾, meaning, while the state is that He knows at every moment ﴿what you do﴾, meaning everything of their deeds that renews, whether it is done from knowledge or from the impulse of desire and natural disposition, whether it is evil or good. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Hafs on the authority of ʿAsim, and Ruways on the authority of Yaʿqub read it in the second person (takhatub), turning the speech away from the third-person absence of the servants, because it is more forceful in warning. The rest read it in the third person (ghaib), in coordination with "the servants," and it is more general and clearer in meaning. Thus His pardoning, together with His knowledge, is out of the vastness of His forbearance.

When He encouraged forgiveness, honour increased, so He said: ﴿And He responds to those who have believed﴾, meaning: the answering of the supplication of those who affirmed faith is found with utmost care and seeking, in everything they ask of Him, or they intercede with Him concerning it, because had He not intended honour for them by means of faith, they would not have believed. He made the verb transitive directly (without a preposition) to draw attention to the increase of His kindness to them and their connection with Him. (p-307) ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, confirming their claim of faith, ﴿and He will give them more﴾, meaning: in addition to what they asked for, He gives them what they did not ask for and what did not occur to their hearts. And since this, although the first [i.e. the former], is an act of His grace, is clearer in showing grace, He said, Exalted is He: ﴿from His bounty﴾, while it is permissible that it be linked to both verbs.

When those whose severance [from Him] had lasted were drawn to union through mention of His honouring them when they turn toward Him, those who persisted in severance were made to fear, so He said: ﴿And the disbelievers﴾, meaning: those deeply rooted in this description, whose deep-rootedness prevented them from repentance and faith, ﴿for them is a severe punishment﴾, and their supplication is not answered. As for others among the disobedient, their punishment is not necessarily bound to being severe. This verse is of *ihtibak* (a rhetorical device of mutual omission): the mention of answering first serves as an indication of its opposite second, and the punishment second serves as an indication of its opposite first. And what delighted him (al-Biqa'i) is that he mentioned both what motivates obedience and what turns away from disobedience.

When the immediate sense of "response" (al-istijaba) would be the provision of everything they asked for in this world, in the way they desired, and what actually exists is otherwise—indeed most of the people of God were constrained—and when granting every request in this abode would in most cases lead to arrogance (al-batar), which leads to misery, thereby producing the opposite of what is intended, He said, by way of excusing His servants—and He is the Supreme King—clarifying that His response is sometimes as the hadith has reported regarding what they asked, sometimes by averting a similar affliction (min al-bala'), and sometimes by deferring it to the Hereafter: ﴿And if﴾, that is, He accepts and responds, while the state is that if ﴿He had expanded﴾ [the provision]... And since this station is great, requiring comprehensive knowledge of their characters and attributes, of what reforms and what corrupts them, and power over every giving and withholding, He expressed it by the Greatest Name, saying: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, who combines all attributes of perfection, drawing attention to the greatness of this station: ﴿the provision﴾ for them. Thus was the original wording, but He disliked that one might suppose this expansion was specific to the penitent, so it was said: ﴿for His servants﴾, that is, all of them, the penitent among them and others, by giving them beyond their need. ﴿They would surely transgress in the earth﴾, that is, they would become people who desire everything they crave; and if He did not permit it, they would strive to bring it about, like kings with the power they possess, by every means that brings them to it, thus multiplying killing, plunder, seizure, beating and similar kinds of corruption. What preceded in Surat al-Nahl regarding discussion of al-baghy (transgression) suffices for mastering the knowledge of this place.

Since the meaning of the speech is that He, glorified is He, does not expand this for them according to what they desire, He built upon it His statement, glorified is He: ﴿But He sends down﴾, that is, for His servants of the provision (﴿with measure﴾), that is, with a determined measure for them as a whole and for each one of them, neither exceeding nor falling short of the measure of its return, ﴿what He wills﴾, of the water which is the origin of provision and the blessings by which He manages His servants, as His wisdom, upon which He established the conditions of this pearl-like order, has required.

Since most people say within themselves: "If He had expanded provision to me, I would have done good, avoided evil, and reformed to the utmost reform," He stated, giving a reason for what He reported, in the style of emphasis: ﴿Indeed He﴾, and the original would have been "with them," but He said: ﴿with His servants﴾, lest it be thought that the matter is specific to those whom He expanded upon or constricted upon: ﴿is All-Aware, All-Seeing﴾, knowing all the outward aspects of their affairs, movements, transitions, and speech, and their inward aspects, so He places each one in what is suitable for him of corruption and reform, transgression and justice, and prepares for everything of that its causes.

When He mentioned the sending down of provision in this manner, and some people, whom misguidance had forsaken, said that rain, plants and the bringing forth of food are merely the habit of time, He made clear that He, glory be to Him, is the One who does this by His power and His will. This is like the sun: He may withhold the rain from its proper season and time, until people despair of it, and then He sends it down if He wills. So He said, using the pronoun that is absent, because the sending down of rain is one of the keys of the Unseen (ﷺ): ﴿And He﴾, meaning none other than Him, is able to do that, for He is the one ﴿who sends down the rain﴾, meaning the rain by which people are given relief, that is, they are answered in what they asked for and are relieved outwardly, just as the Revelation is sent down, by which they are relieved outwardly and inwardly.

Since the sending down does not occupy the whole time of despair, He introduced the preposition and said: ﴿after they have despaired﴾, meaning they lost hope of its being sent down and knew that none other than Him could send it down, and none other is aimed at in it, so that this would be more inciting for them to give thanks. This was the original wording, but when He made clear that it is rain, He said, as an explanation that it is mercy and as a generalization of its effect to plants and other things: ﴿and spreads His mercy﴾, meaning over the plain and the mountain. So from the clouds carried by the wind there comes down water that fills the earth, to the extent that if all creatures gathered to bear it they could not carry it. Thus the earth becomes pools and rivers, plants, herbage, trees, grain, fruits, and other benefits, small and great. Glory be to God, how sublime is this overpowering power and this manifest sign! From the earth, which in its hardness is such that picks cannot break it, there comes forth herbage which in its softness is softer than silk, in its delicacy more delicate than the breeze, and branches from the trunks of trees, in which the beaks of birds bend, more delicate than the tongues of sparrows. How contemptible is the one who denies His bringing forth of the dead from the graves, or who turns away from this by some kind of delusion!

When He had earlier denied them the taking of any protector other than Him, by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or have they taken protectors besides Him?﴾ [Ash-Shura: 9], and established that He is the Protector, and made Himself known to them through His signs, which contain the marvels of His lights, and all of which are in the utmost perfection, requiring praise that is continuous in its pattern, He said: ﴿And He﴾, meaning He alone, not another, ﴿is the Protector﴾, meaning the One nearer to His servants than anyone else in anything, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾, meaning the One who deserves all the qualities of praise, although He praises whoever obeys Him, so He increases him from His bounty, and He always joins His rope to the one who holds fast to His rope.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 29:

Since what has preceded of the expansion and contraction of provision, and the sending down and withholding of rain, are among the great signs, he generalized by mentioning something of that which is a part of it, and this (generalization) indicates all that the preceding verse ended with of praise (*hamd*), which is the attribute of possessing all the qualities of perfection. He said, conjoining (*'aṭifan*) to what is implied: "That is among the signs of God that point to His power and His choice, and that He is the One who gives life to this existence, by meanings from the spirit of revelation and other things at times, and by bodies from water and other things at other times: ﴿And among His signs﴾, the great ones that show this and His deserving of all the qualities of perfection, ﴿is the creation of the heavens﴾, which you know to be many, by what you see of the matters of the stars, ﴿and the earth﴾, meaning its kind, in the forms it has and with the benefits and goods it contains, ﴿and what He has scattered﴾, meaning what He has dispersed, with bodies and hearts, in this wondrous pattern of sensation and movement by choice, along with the variation in shapes, natures, forms, characters and other things of deficiency and perfection."

Since the earth is a building and the sky its roof, whoever is in one of the two is correctly described as being in each of them: low by being humbled, and high by being shaded. He, exalted, said: ﴿in them﴾, meaning the heavens and the earth, especially since He made for each of them a means (*tasabbuban*) in this (matter), by what He deposited in them of substances and what He produced from them of elements. (p-313)

Since life, which is the cause of spreading out and creeping about, may perhaps leave its possessor with pride and harshness in himself, so that we imagine him to have complete power, He made it feminine (*anna-tha*) to belittle his power and to show his rank and station as lowly, and so He diminished (*qallala*) ﴿of a creature﴾, meaning something which has the capacity to move by life, from among humans, jinn, angels and the rest of the animals, with their differing kinds, colours, shapes, languages, natures, species, types, regions, directions and lands. Whoever looks at His handiwork, glorified is He, becomes certain of His existence, power and choice. Then, if he looks deeply and follows contemplation in reflection, he reaches knowledge of the Creator by His names and attributes, and what befits Him and what is impossible for Him. So he praises Him with praises that have no end, and glorifies Him with His glory. Then if he looks more deeply, he rises to understand the wisdom of what the messengers brought and the books sent down.

Since we know that whoever brings things into existence, gathering their scattered parts whenever He wills, despite the deficiency of control and the weakness in turning them, we are worthy of definite knowledge (p-314) of the content of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He﴾, meaning with what He has of attributes of majesty by which He knows the apparent, while the hidden is greater for us, ﴿is over their gathering﴾, meaning these creatures, of those with minds and others, after their dispersal in hearts and bodies by death and other things, by desires, passions and other such things.

Since gathering is necessary, He expressed it with the particle of certainty (*adāt al-taḥaqquq*), so He said, attaching it to the gathering: ﴿when﴾, and He affirmed the view toward the resurrection, so He expressed it with the present tense, saying: ﴿He wills; He is All-Powerful﴾, meaning fully capable, just as He was fully capable at the time of origination from non-existence, by gathering them in one plain, where the caller makes them hear and the sight reaches them,

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 30:

When He (glorified is He) had reminded them of His blessings, and the context was enumerating what is fitting to the aim of this surah among them, the mind was apt to conceive of what exists in this world of illnesses, afflictions, sorrows and anxieties, and of the misery and happiness it brings. So He said, healing the confusion of their question about that by explaining what is in it of His blessing, in a manner that indicates the completeness of His power, joining it to what is implied by what preceded, with the implied sense: "He is the One who created you and provided for you, and He is the one who disposes of you after your dispersal, through well-being and affliction, with complete disposal. So there is no blessing (p-315) with you nor any calamity except from Him, and its possessors cannot avert it nor avert any part of it. He alone is your Guardian." ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you﴾ — He addressed them directly, for added closeness to the obedient and rebuke to the disobedient, and He generalized with His saying ﴿of an affliction﴾, and He related the predicate of the subject with His saying ﴿it is because of﴾, meaning: it is occurring because of that which — this is according to the reading of Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir, while the rest read with the fa' affirmed, for added clarity of the causal relation. So they read "fa-bi-ma" because the subject includes the meaning of a conditional, i.e., "so it is by means of that which."

Since souls are naturally disposed toward opposites, they cannot be freed from them except by a mighty help from God, and since their whole action, or most of it, is upon them, He expressed it with the bare verb, as an indication of this, saying: ﴿earned﴾.

Since action is mostly done by the hand, He said: ﴿your hands﴾, meaning: of sins. So every affliction that reaches a person is only because of a previous sin, the least of which is negligence. Ibn Majah in his Sunan, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and al-Hakim (the wording is his), who said: "its chain is sound," narrated from Thawban (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Nothing averts the decree except supplication, and nothing increases life except righteousness, and a man is indeed deprived of provision because of a sin he commits."

So the verse calls every person, at the occurrence of an affliction, to hasten to self-examination, so that he knows from where his negligence came, (p-316) and then hastens to repentance from it and turning to Allah, to save his soul from destruction. The benefit of this, although everything is by His creation and will, is the manifestation of humility and submission, the sensing of need and dependence upon the One, the Subduer. Were it not for the revelation of the Shari'ah, no path to guidance would be found, nor to these wondrous perfections. Such admonitions are to draw out from the servant what He deposited in his nature and fixed in his disposition, like planting and sowing that water and sunlight have reached, to bring forth what He deposited in his nature of divine knowledge and lofty wisdom.

When He mentioned His justice, He followed it with His grace, saying: ﴿and He pardons much﴾. Were it not for His pardon and forgiveness, He would not leave upon its back a single creature. This also includes what afflicts the righteous, to attain ranks, virtues and special distinctions that they could not reach except through it, because their deeds did not reach them; so it is the best arrival from Allah to them. It was said to Abu Sulayman al-Darani: "What is the matter with the wise, that they remove blame from one who wronged them?" He said: "Because they know that Allah tested them with their sins," and he recited this verse.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 31:

When one who punishes with something short of death may perhaps think that he is powerless, He said: ﴿And you cannot escape (Allah)﴾ — even if He wished to destroy you entirely, and [even if He wished] anything at all from you, whatever it may be. And since one whose power is established over the place of exaltedness, through His creation and what He has deposited in the created things, is more worthy of power over what is below it, He indicated this by His saying: ﴿on earth﴾. And since the discussion concerns punishment in this world before death, and no one claims there the ability to reach the heavens, no caller called to mention it, unlike what preceded in al-'Ankabut. And since He negated their being able to escape by themselves, and He, glory be to Him, has such exaltedness that minds fall short of it, so that everything is beneath Him, and He is able over everything, He said: ﴿And you have not﴾, that is, when gathered together, so how when alone.

And since the ranks are at the utmost lowliness relative to His rank, and humility is beneath His presence, He affirmed the preposition, alerting to this, and said: ﴿besides Allah﴾, that is, the One who encompasses everything in greatness, majesty and might. And He generalized by His saying: ﴿any protector﴾, that is, one who would be in charge of any of your affairs independently, ﴿nor any helper﴾ who would repel from you anything He, glory be to Him, wills for you.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 32:

When Allah (Subhanahu wa Ta'ala) demonstrated the completeness of His power and His will, and concluded with the negation of a partner, which is necessarily entailed by His oneness (wahdaniyyah), the belief in which is the foundation of righteous deeds, He demonstrated it by the greatest of signs in their estimation, the clearest of them in their own selves, and the closest of them to their understanding, because of their sincerity (ikhlas) when they are in it. So He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And among His signs﴾, meaning those that indicate the completeness of His power, His will, His oneness, and the greatness of His dominion: His subjugation and taming of the ships' course (sayr al-Fulk) upon it, carrying what no other than them can carry, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿the ships (al-jawar)﴾, meaning the ships, and it is among the adjectives that have taken the place of nouns (ajra majra al-a'lam). The qualified noun was left out because what follows it indicates it; therefore it was omitted. The rule is that when an adjective does not specify its noun, omitting the noun is not permitted, so we say: "I passed by an engineer (muhandis)," and we do not say: "I passed by one who walks (mashin)," except with a qualifying indication, as here.

When they were heavy in themselves, and what is placed in them of loads would weigh down mountains, and every heavy thing has of its own nature only sinking into water, they were as though they were in the water and not upon it, because they are deserving of drowning. So He, the Exalted, said, warning against His seizures, reminding of the magnificence of His blessing, and informing of the reality of the ships (al-jawari): ﴿in the sea like mountains (al-a'lam)﴾, meaning towering mountains, with what they have of height in themselves above the water, then with what carries them and the sail upon them of elevation. Al-Khalil said: everything that is elevated among the Arabs is called 'alam (a landmark).

(p-319) When it was as if it were said, "And what are those signs?", he mentioned what should make them fear them and informs them that everything He has permitted them of their affairs is only by His power and His choice. So He said: ﴿If He wills﴾, that is, Allah, who carries you in them upon the surface of the water, a clear sign whose consideration has fallen away from you because of your intense preoccupation with it, ﴿He stills the wind﴾ which He drives, while you acknowledge that its command is in no one's hand but His. ﴿So they become still﴾, that is, as a consequence, they (the ships) become still, meaning they stay standing, whether by night or by day. Perhaps he expressed it with this verb (*yaẓlalna*, "they become still") although its basic sense is standing still by day, because the day is the place of ability over things and is the one awaited by everyone struggling to remove his hardship and ease his affair. ﴿Motionless﴾, that is, fixed and steady, without movement, ﴿upon its surface﴾, a manifest steadiness. This is indicated by the affirmation of the two *lāms* (in *yaẓlalna*, read as *yaẓlalna* with both *lāms* written and pronounced) and the opening of its first *lām* for all readers.

Since this is the locus of their sincerity in calling upon Allah and turning away from partners, they used to say in such a situation: "Be sincere, for your gods, that is, the idols and others besides Allah, do not avail anything at sea." They used to ascribe partners to Him in that, yet when they came out safely to land, they were in the position of one who does not regard that as a sign at all. Therefore He emphasized His statement: ﴿Indeed in that﴾, that is, in what He mentioned of the state of the ships in their movement and their stillness, things that none can do except Allah, glorified is He, as evidenced by the consensus of all people on turning to Him alone in that matter and detaching from anything other than Him, ﴿are signs﴾, that is, that His encompassing of all attributes of perfection is a matter fixed in minds and established in the original innate nature (*al-fiṭar al-ūlā*), which nothing turns away from except caprice, and that the invalidity of any other being's claim to such things is so evident that it cannot be unknown.

Since they used to praise one another for patience in the face of the calamities of events and gratitude for every favor, and used to disparage one another for impatience and ingratitude, and since this requires their steadfastness in one state, then if the truth lay with their objects of worship, their turning away from them in times of hardship would be something no one of perfect men would approach or even glance at, those who avoid disgrace and who do not adopt the mark of those immersed in shame. And if the truth is as it truly is, that it belongs to Allah, then their turning away from Him in times of ease, after He has favored them by saving them from hardship, is something no person of resolve would do. Alluding to this with the two intensive forms, He said: ﴿For every steadfast one (*ṣabbār*)﴾, that is, in hardship, ﴿grateful (*shakūr*)﴾, that is, in ease, even if those who oppose him are many and their dispute against him is great. These two qualities are those of the sincere believer who has devoted his resolve to contemplating the signs; he derives lessons from them and, through them, polishes the eye of sight with the light of insight.

(p-321) When he had alerted, through this parenthetical insertion between the conditional clause and its conjoined element, to the subtle meanings within its sublime expressions, he said, completing what this contains of encouragement in the form of warning: ﴿Or﴾, i.e., or if He wills, at any time He wishes. He attributed the wrecking (al-iyba') to the ships (al-jawari) to emphasize the generality of the will regarding the destruction of the passengers, so He said: ﴿He destroys them﴾, i.e., He destroys them by drowning, through sending the wind and other calamities (al-tabariih), until they are, after that height, in their pit (waqb), i.e., their hollows, and sink into the water and its depths. The verification of the meaning of "wabaqa" in all its inflections has already been given in Surat al-Kahf. Among its meanings: wabaqa, like wa'ada, wajila and wariha, wubuqan and mawbaqan, means "to perish," and al-mawbiq, on the pattern of majlis, means "that which destroys," and anything that stands between two things, because the pit (al-waqba) intervenes between what is in it and other than it. From this it is said of the appointed place (al-maw'id): mawbiq. And awbaqahu means: he imprisoned him or he destroyed him.

Since the destruction of them (the ships) is a destruction of the passengers, He said, clarifying that they are the intended ones, using the verb alone, as an indication that the son of Adam, because of the deficiencies he has been created with (p-322), does not have from himself any act free of the taint of deficiency, urging him to take refuge in God for the refinement of his self and the sincerity of his action: ﴿for what they have earned﴾, i.e., for what they did of disobediences through their diligence and striving in it.

Since the implied meaning, as an elaboration of the wrecking, is: "so everyone in them drowns if He wills, and many of them drown if He wills," He conjoined to it His saying: ﴿and He pardons﴾, i.e., if He wills, ﴿many﴾, i.e., of the people who are in these destructive ships, so He saves them by swimming, or by being carried on a plank, or otherwise. And if He wills, He sends the wind gentle, so it carries them and brings them to the furthest desired destination, and other such possibilities falling under His will. The verb, as you see, is conjoined to "yubiq" and was conjoined with "wa" because it is a division of the two conditions of the wrecking. It has the meaning of what is transmitted from the people of Medina regarding the accusative reading of "yaʿfu" by supposing an implied "in" (if), so that the meaning becomes: He causes a wrecking and a pardoning.

[p. 323] When all of this is in the form of a test, whoever will not gain insight so that his sincerity endures, and whoever returns to blindness will not attain deliverance, He said, clarifying with the accusative (*naṣb*) for the turning away (*ṣarf*) from coordination with any of the preceding verbs, because the meaning would be corrupted by their being within the scope of the condition, so that knowledge too becomes conditional: ﴿And that those who dispute concerning Our signs may know﴾, that is, at the time of deliverance through pardon. Since the station of greatness is strongly incompatible with disputation, He turned the speech to it and said: ﴿concerning Our signs﴾, that is, these signs, which cannot be compared to their greatness nor measured against their majesty and might, returning to what they were upon of polytheism and contention regarding complete power by denying resurrection. From the *waw* of turning (*wāw al-ṣarf*) one knows that what follows it is a singular noun in the sense of a verbal noun (*mufrad fī ta'wīl al-maṣdar*), because the accusative after it is by the implicit *an*, so it becomes a subject (*mubtada'*) whose predicate is what the context indicates. The estimate here is: "and His knowledge, glory be to Him, of the disputants is present at this." Expressing it with the imperfect verb indicates continuity, since the connection of knowledge is renewed with every disputant whenever disputation occurs. The reading of Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir with the nominative (*raf'*) indicates this, for the estimate is: "and He knows," so the nominative and the accusative are the same here.

Al-Radi said in his commentary on Ibn al-Hajib's statement concerning the particles that govern the verb (*nawāṣib al-fi'l*): "The *fa'* (meaning governing) is with two conditions: causation (*al-sababiyya*), and that before it be one of the eight items, and the *waw* that occurs after the condition and before the response, such as: *in ta'tinī fa-tukrimanī* (if you come to me and so you honor me) or *aw tukrimunī anta* (or you honor me), or after the condition and the response: *in ta'tinī innaka fa-ukrimka* (if you come to me, indeed you, and I will honor you) or *wa-ukrimka* (and I will honor you). This is because the condition in the first case and the response in the second resemble negation, since the response is conditional and its existence depends on the existence of the condition, while the existence of the condition is assumed, so neither of the two is described as existing in reality." On this is based the saying of Him, exalted is He: ﴿and that those who﴾ in the reading of the accusative. Then he said: "Likewise one says regarding the verb in the accusative after the *waw* of turning, that when they intended in it the sense of collectivity (*al-jam'iyya*), they put the imperfect in the accusative after it, so that the turning away from the usual course of the preceding speech would guide from the outset that it is not for coordination. Thus it is either the *waw* of circumstance (*wāw al-ḥāl*), and its most frequent occurrence is before a nominal sentence, so the imperfect after it is in the estimate of a subject whose predicate is necessarily omitted, so the meaning of *qum wa-aqūmu* (stand and I stand) is: *qum wa-qiyāmī thābit* (stand, and my standing is established), that is, in the state of the establishment of my standing. As for the meaning of *ma'a* (with), which does not occur except before a noun, they intended here the accompaniment of one verb with another, the verb after it being in the accusative, so the meaning of *qum wa-aqūmu* is: *qum ma'a qiyāmī* (stand with my standing), just as they intended in the object of accompaniment (*al-maf'ūl ma'ahu*) the accompaniment of noun with noun, so they put in the accusative what follows the *waw*. If we made the *waw* coordinating for the verbal noun derived from the verb before it, the deliverance would be taken from it, that is, there was no standing from you and standing from me, it would not have in it an explicit indication of the sense of collectivity. The better course, in intending explicitness regarding something in the sense of making it appear in a manner clear regarding what they intended to make explicit, is ...."
