Then, concerning the particle of causation: they stipulated for the accusative after the *fa'* of causation that what precedes it be one of the mentioned items, namely the command, the prohibition, the negation, the interrogation, the wish, the offer, the urging, and the hope, because these are not of established occurrence, so they are like the condition which is not certain to occur, and what follows the *fa'* is like its response. Then they applied to what precedes the *waw* of collectivity the requirement that one of the mentioned items be present, as with what precedes the *fa'* of causation, which is more frequently used than the *waw* in this kind of position, I mean in the accusative of the imperfect after it, because of the resemblance of the *waw* to the *fa'* in the basic function of coordination, and in turning what follows them both from the usual course of coordination, for the intent of causation in one and collectivity in the other, and because collectivity is close to succession, which is a necessary consequence of causation." Then he said: "Likewise, perhaps the *waw* of circumstance does not turn, as the imperfect may come after it affirmatively, as we mentioned in the chapter on circumstance, such as *qumtu wa-aḍribu Zaydan* (I stood and I strike Zayd), that is, *wa-anā aḍribu Zaydan* (while I am striking Zayd)."

Since the knowledge of the Capable (*al-Qādir*) of disobedience necessitates the punishment of whoever disobeyed Him, it was as if it were said: "Indeed they have lost by doing that; so would that I knew what their state will be." He answered with His saying: ﴿They have no escape﴾, that is, no refuge or place of flight at all from His punishment, nor by any slight thing, even if the infliction of punishment upon them seems delayed in your view. His punishment, glory be to Him, has an inward aspect, which is gradual leading (*al-istidrāj*) through blessings, and this is not perceived except by the masters of hearts, who are brought near in the presence of the Knower of the unseen. It also has an outward aspect. It is permissible that ﴿those who﴾ be the subject (*fā'il*) of ﴿knows﴾, and in that case this clause is in the place of the accusative, as it takes the place of the object of knowledge.

When he knew that all blessings, including rain and its effects and the dispersal of animals on land and sea, are exposed to cessation, and that the world is subject to great fluctuations and dreadful conditions, he therefore said, belittling their worldly life and the splendor in it, with its swift withering, cessation, setting and departure, and telling them that, together with what was mentioned, they have no power over any of it except that it dies. He bestows it upon them. As for them, they are a weak people who have no power over anything and have nothing of their own except incapacity. If they reasoned, they would know, and if they knew, they would act like slaves and obey the Strong, the Mighty. ﴿So whatever you have been given﴾, i.e., O people, ﴿of a thing﴾, i.e., of the apparent blessings. The conditional "mā" is answered by His saying: ﴿then it is the enjoyment of the life of this world﴾, i.e., the near, base life, in which there is no benefit for anyone (p-327) except for the duration of his life. That is deserving of turning away from it and from the deeds it causes, except what brings one closer to God. ﴿And what is with God﴾, i.e., and that which is. He shifted the speech from the manifestation of majesty to something greater than it by mentioning the all-comprehensive Name, to encourage remembrance of the effects of the attributes of beauty and to warn against the effects of the attributes of majesty. So he said: ﴿is with God﴾, i.e., the Greatest King, who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, from the blessings of both abodes ﴿is better﴾, i.e., in itself, and far better than purely worldly blessings, because their benefit is cut off.

Since worldly blessings may accompany a person throughout his life and thus lead to lasting, He said: ﴿and more enduring﴾, i.e., than the worldly ones, because they must be taken from him by death. For this reason He restricted it to life, so that one does not prefer what is perishable, despite its baseness, over what endures, despite its preciousness.

Having explained its preciousness to encourage desire for it, he identified its recipients, saying: ﴿for those who have faith﴾, i.e., who brought this truth into being ﴿and upon﴾, i.e., and while they affirm it, that they are upon, and he shifted the speech to the attribute of excellence (ihsan), because it is the most fitting attribution for one who relies upon God (tawakkul). He stressed the matter by the addition, pointing to "it is excellence," which is most suitable to their condition, so he said: ﴿their Lord﴾, i.e., the One from whom they have never seen excellence except from Him alone, through what He nurtured in them of sincerity toward Him, ﴿they rely upon﴾, i.e., they entrust all their affairs to Him, as others entrust their goods to one whom they perceive to have the strength to carry them, and they do not turn to anything other than Him at all, so that through this the hidden polytheism (shirk) is negated from them, just as overt polytheism was negated by faith. The expression with the particle of elevation (ʿalā) is a figure for attribution and committing oneself to Him, since carrying something upon Him is clearer in ease and further from worry and hardship. Perhaps the expression in the present tense is to lighten the matter of tawakkul, by renewing contentment with it whenever a matter arises. Whoever is like this, God suffices him in every difficulty. Thus they share with the people of the world in obtaining its blessings, and differ from them in that their Lord, glory be to Him, makes them in a manner for which there is no reckoning against them, and rather they have in them rewards that bring about bliss and joy. They also differ in that He makes these blessings sufficient for their needs and a cushion for their hardships, and He increases them in the enduring good deeds, from which the bliss of the Hereafter follows after the ease of this world.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 37:

Since both faith (īmān) and reliance upon God (tawakkul) are inward matters, they must have outward evidences in visible deeds. Clearing oneself of vices (takhliyāt) and adorning oneself with virtues (taḥliyāt) are both required, and clearing away vices takes precedence over adorning oneself with virtues, because clearing away vices is a warding off of corruptions (mafāsid), whereas adorning oneself is a bringing about of benefits (maṣāliḥ). He said, coordinating with "those who" (alladhīna): ﴿And those who avoid﴾, meaning they impose upon themselves the obligation to be made to avoid, ﴿the major sins (kabā'ir al-ithm)﴾, meaning the class of great acts, which do not exist except within their individual instances, and by which a defilement comes upon the soul, thereby necessitating punishment for it together with the body. He coordinated upon "major" the phrase: ﴿and the indecencies (al-fawāḥish)﴾, which are what the Sharia, reason and natural disposition deem abominable, and which are the three signs of God (āyāt Allāh), whose establishment is a proof against His servants, and to Him belongs the conclusive proof. So people have magnified their matter, and even if they were minor sins, because they indicate a breach of manliness (murū'ah), such as stealing a morsel of food, and acknowledging disobedience in the presence of an elderly person of great standing to one who neither fears nor hopes in him. Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī read kabīr (singular), and it is for the genus, so it carries the meaning of the plural reading, or it is more eloquent because it encompasses the singular.

When he mentioned what desires may lead to without the restraint of overpowering anger, he said, drawing attention to its greatness, expressing with the particle of certainty (ḥarf al-taḥqīq) to indicate that there is no alternative to it, to settle the soul upon it, linking it to the verb of forgiveness: ﴿And when﴾, and he emphasized it with His saying: ﴿what﴾, and he placed anger first, as a sign of concern for extinguishing its ember and cooling its heat, so He said: ﴿they are angered﴾, meaning anger which is genuine, arising from a matter that customarily provokes anger, and He made clear by the separating pronoun (ḍamīr al-faṣl) that their inner states in forgiving are like their outward ones, so He said: ﴿they forgive﴾, meaning, by counting and concealing, that whenever anger renews itself in them, they renew forgiveness, that is, erasing the sin both in its essence and its trace, while having the power to take revenge. Their dispositions thus require pardon rather than retaliation, so long as there is no transgression (baghy) from the wrongdoer, for one is not held to account merely for anger except an arrogant person, and arrogance is not fitting for anyone other than God. This is because what clouds the forbearance of others at the intensity of a matter, such as the recklessness of ignorance and the foolishness of opinion, does not cloud theirs. Thus it shows that forgiving without anger is not considered in comparison with forgiving while angry. In the Ṣaḥīḥ: "He, may God bless him and grant him peace, never took revenge for himself, except when the sanctities of God were violated." Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibrāhīm, who said: "The believers used to dislike being humiliated, and when they were able, they pardoned."

When he had completed what concerns adorning oneself with virtue (*al-tahalli*, the adornment of the soul with good qualities), he followed it with what concerns emptying oneself of vice (*al-takhalli*, the purging of the soul of blameworthy qualities). He mentioned four attributes, which are the foundations of equity (*al-nasafa*). Whatever is built upon them, even a quarter of it, its practitioners become like a single body, and no calamity seizes them in this world or the Hereafter. So He said: ﴿And those who respond to their Lord﴾, meaning those who bring about the response with what they have of knowledge that guides to the path of right direction, ﴿to their Lord﴾, meaning the One who calls them to respond to Him, by His benevolence toward them in bringing them into being, out of the intensity with which they compel their souls toward it. They seek it from themselves with a great and sincere seeking, such that no soul of any of them remains, nor any remnant of illusion or trace, except in accordance with the pleasure of Him, glorified is He, because they know that He has called them to it while He is their Cultivator, for their righteousness, their happiness, and their success, since He is all-encompassing in knowledge and intensely merciful, and is never suspected in any way whatsoever.

Since this is general for every good to which He, glorified is He, has called, He singled out the greatest of the bodily acts of worship and increased its greatness by expressing it with the word "establishing," so He said: ﴿And they establish﴾, meaning with what they have of strength, ﴿the prayer﴾. The definite article together with the word indicates that they brought its form into being, carried by its spirit, in a manner that requires its continuance always.

Since the response necessitates the unity of hearts through faith, which necessitates unity in words and deeds, and the prayer necessitates unity of bodies, He mentioned unity in words (p-332), which, for those of perfection, results in unity in deeds. So He said, expressing it by the nominal sentence to urge that they make this a stable disposition that does not part from them: ﴿And their affair﴾, meaning everything that befalls them of what requires them to deliberate, ﴿is by consultation (shura)﴾, meaning they consult with one another about it in a great consultation, exerting in it what they have of inner strength and purity in sincerity and counsel. It is from *al-shawr*, which is presenting and displaying. ﴿Among themselves﴾, meaning that in the state of consultation there is no distinction between the elder among them and the younger; rather each of them listens to the speech of the other and examines its soundness and its flaws by applying it to the principles and branches of the Sacred Law. None of them therefore holds to an opinion persistently, because he is constantly suspicious of his own opinion, having realized his deficiency compared with the abundance of knowledge and clarity of understanding that the other possesses. They do not rush into anything; rather, deliberation has become a disposition for them. The setting of this verse, in the context of consultation, indicates the great benefit of consultation and the magnitude of its usefulness. Al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "No people consult together except that they are guided to the most rightful of their affairs." Yet al-Tabarani narrated in *al-Saghir* and *al-Awsat*, but with a weak chain, on the authority of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He who seeks guidance does not fail, he who consults does not regret, and he who is moderate does not become poor." And he narrated in *al-Awsat* on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever intends a matter and consults a Muslim man about it, Allah grants him success in the most rightful of his affair." (p-333)

Since sharing wealth, after unity in words and agreement in deeds, is the greatest comprehensive gathering of praiseworthy qualities, and the clearest indication of what he claimed of unity in state and outcome, He said, making the matter of it easy for them, that in reality they have no role in obtaining it, being pleased with them for a little of it: ﴿And from what﴾, and He turned the speech to the locus of greatness, reminding them of what they customarily recognize among themselves, that there is no hope of drawing near to the great except through gifts. So He said: ﴿We have provided them﴾, meaning by Our greatness, without any power or strength from them, ﴿they spend﴾, meaning they continually spend, out of generosity from them, even if what is in their hands is little, relying on the bounty of Allah, glorified and exalted is He. They do not withhold their hands as the hypocrites do. That spending is in accordance with what We have specified for them. So they share with others by consultation from the excess of their intellects, and by spending from the excess of their wealth, out of piety from them and vigilance before Allah, not out of the desire of the self.

(p-٣٣٤) Since punishment contains both benefit and harm, He (glory be to Him) urged forgiveness, giving priority to averting harm. A person, because he does not know hearts, is by no means correct to be punished merely out of anger, for he may err and punish one who angered him. And he (the one being forgiven) is of noble essence, generous disposition, high in aspiration, and proud of soul. The sin that angered him was only an unintentional error that is pardoned, or he was lied about in it, so he nurtures in his soul its sister, which corrupts relations among people, and it leads to great ruin. Persistence in pardoning brings about corruption and emboldens people in obstinacy. Baghy (transgression), meaning persistence in evil, realizes the intent of the wrongdoing and permits proceeding to retaliation. Taking revenge against wicked people may, together with strength of heart, sometimes require spending money. After mentioning spending, he praised victory with His words: ﴿Those who﴾. He used the particle of certainty to indicate that its condition must occur either in fact or in potential. He then said, governing the verb of victory and placing first what the soul is concerned to repel because it cannot bear it: ﴿when oppression (al-baghy) afflicts them﴾, that is, befalls them and has an effect on them. Baghy is persistence in hurling evil. ﴿They﴾, that is, by themselves specifically, because of the strength of heart and firmness that makes known that the forgiveness he granted earlier was only due to their elevated standing, not their lowliness. ﴿Defend themselves﴾, that is, they deliver retaliation, with the intelligence, strength of grip, and firmness of heart that God gave them, in its proper place, in the manner that is fitting for restraining the transgressor from repeating against them and (p-٣٣٥) from daring against others, repeating this whenever he repeats against them. This is part of reconciling relations among people. They are neither helpless nor lax in the matter of their religion. The expression of these verbs with plural attribution indicates that the deterrent empowerment is not complete except with collective action, and whoever is alone in these matters, his concern is prolonged and his grief is great. Al-Nakha'i said: They disliked to humiliate themselves, lest the wicked become emboldened against them.

Since permission to retaliate in this context of praise would make it appealing, given what the soul naturally inclines to, he first restrained the one who has a heart by holding him back from unrestrained pursuit and confining him to the limit of equivalence. Second, he called it an evil (sayyi'a, "evil"), even though it was by way of mushakala (correspondence in form). Third, he urged pardon. Thus the praiseworthy kind of retaliation becomes only that which is for raising the Word of God, with no admixture of the self at all. So He said: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾, meaning whatever evil it was, ﴿an evil like it﴾, meaning it does not exceed it in form or in meaning at all. These sentences secured, in the best manner, a call to the three mothers of virtues: knowledge, chastity and courage (p-336). Thus the praise of responding and of prayer is a call to knowledge, the praise of spending is a call to chastity, and the praise of retaliation is a call to courage, so that no one supposes that their submission to what has passed was mere humiliation. The restriction to equivalence is a call to the virtue that distributes justice among all, which is justice ('adl). This last is inclusive of the three virtues, for whoever knows equivalence is knowledgeable, whoever intends to stop at it is chaste, and whoever restrains himself to it is courageous. It has also become clear, from the praise of retaliation following the praise of forgiveness, that the first is for the one who is powerless and the second is for the one who prevails and is arrogant, as indicated by the word "transgression" (baghy).

Since the condition of equivalence was an urging, after the legislating of justice, which is retribution (qisas), toward pardon, which is the decisive settlement (fasl), because truly attaining equivalence by a servant, who is characterized by weakness, hardly exists, He stated as a consequence: ﴿But whoever forgives﴾, meaning by waiving his entire right or by reducing from it, so that he may be cleared of what is forbidden in transgression. ﴿And makes reconciliation﴾, meaning he brings about reconciliation among people through pardon and reform, and reforms himself, so that God may reform what is between him and the people. Thus he is, by that, one who avenges himself for himself. ﴿His reward is upon God﴾, meaning the One who encompasses all attributes of perfection. So He gives him according to what the meaning of this supreme Name requires. This is the secret of turning the speech toward Him rather than toward the manifestation of greatness. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God does not increase a servant by pardon except in honor."

Since this was an urging toward pardon after praising retaliation, he made clear that its reason is the disliking of placing something in other than its proper place, because no one knows the equivalence in that matter except God. So He said, using the pronoun to indicate that equivalence belongs to the hidden unseen, emphasizing the restraint of the self from the great excess of pursuit in retaliation: ﴿Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers﴾, meaning He does not honor those who place a thing in other than its proper place, in the manner of one who walks along the path of derivation when he is deeply versed in that, whether it is initiated or exceeds the bounds in revenge by taking vengeance.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 41:**

When this statement closed the door on retaliation, given the sense the wronged person feels that he has been wronged by everyone, he said, emphatically negating this impression: ﴿And whoever retaliates after he has been wronged﴾, i.e., strives to defend himself with his effort ﴿after his wrong﴾, i.e., after another has wronged him, and not intending to stray from his right, even if his retaliation extended over the entire period of his straying.

When Allah, exalted is He, had explained the status of the one who looks after the interests of the servants, who has stripped himself of his own self-interest out of benevolence toward the servants of Allah, and is of the highest rank, He explained the status of the one who defends himself, who intends to heal his chest and remove his rage. He said, linking the response to the cause with the particle (فاء, fa', "so/then") as an explanation of the shortcoming of his view in merely repelling injustice from himself. It is permissible for ﴿مِن﴾ (min, "whoever") to be a relative pronoun (ism mawsul, a relative word) with the (فاء) because the relative pronoun has a resemblance to the conditional (شرط, shart, "conditional particle").

When He first expressed it in the singular, it might have been restricted to one person, lest the trial become great. He then used the plural to indicate that the trial lies only in endorsing injustice, not in supporting the wronged person, whether he is one or many. He said: ﴿Those﴾, i.e., those who retaliate, only to repel the oppressor's injustice from themselves ﴿—there is no ground against them﴾, and He emphasized this by affirming the preposition, saying: ﴿no path [of blame]﴾, i.e., no punishment and no reproach.

Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "I did not know until Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her, entered upon me without permission, angry. Then she came toward me, and I turned away from her, until the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Go ahead and retaliate against her.' So I turned toward her until I saw that her saliva had dried up in her mouth, and she could not return a single word to me. Then I saw the face of the Prophet (ﷺ) brighten."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 42:

When He negated the way (sabil) against him, after the listener's eagerness to learn the place of what the preceding speech had hinted at of wrongdoing (zulm), He clarified that, saying: ﴿Indeed, the way is only against﴾ — i.e., the path that leads to no prevention at all, by hardship and distress — ﴿those who wrong people﴾ — He used the plural to inform of the great number of corrupters, so as to embolden [the believers] to take retribution against them, even though they are many — for Allah forsakes them. So He said: ﴿who wrong people﴾, i.e., they inflict their wrongdoing upon them deliberately, with aggression. ﴿And commit excess﴾, i.e., they transgress the limits ﴿in the earth﴾, by that which corrupts it after its reform, having prepared it for goodness in nature, deed, knowledge and action. And since an act may be transgression (baghy) even when accompanied by a right, such as retaliation that is combined with exceeding its limit in it, He said: ﴿without right﴾, i.e., the complete right. And since He established by this speech the way against them, the listener would be inclined to ask about it, so He said: ﴿Those — for them is a painful punishment﴾, i.e., they are the hateful, the distant from Allah. Painful: i.e., causing pain, in return for the pain they inflicted upon those among Allah's servants whom they wronged, such that its pain encompasses their bodies and their spirits, with whatever apparent and hidden perceptions they possess.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 43:

When the context of this speech and its arrangement made clear that the implied meaning is: "Whoever is patient and refrains from retaliating is in a better state than the one who retaliates, because error in pardoning is more preferable than error in retaliation," He added, emphasizing what the context had also made clear about the praise of the one who retaliates: ﴿And whoever is patient﴾ — refraining from retaliation without vengeance or complaint (p-340) ﴿and forgives﴾ — so he explicitly dropped punishment and reproach, and thus erased the very trace and mark of the sin. ﴿Indeed, that﴾ — i.e., that act which proceeds from him, which is supremely exalted and cannot be described — ﴿is of the steadfast resolve of affairs﴾ — i.e., the affairs which, by virtue of their being fit to be resolved upon, have in themselves become as though they were the very essence of resolve, or are qualified to be resolved upon what one wills. "Resolve" (al-'azm) is undertaking a matter after deliberation and reflection. Abu 'Ali ibn al-Farra' said: The verses of pardon are to be understood as referring to the wrongdoer who regrets, and the verses praising retaliation refer to the one who persists, and that is only praised together with the ability to achieve complete victory, as Yusuf, peace be upon him, said to his brothers:

﴿No reproach shall be upon you today; may Allah forgive you﴾ [Yusuf: 92]. And he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) did so on many occasions, among them the greatest standing he took on the day of the Conquest at the door of the Ka'bah, when he said to the Quraysh, who were beneath him like drenched sheep: "What do you think I will do with you, O assembly of Quraysh?" They said: "Good; a noble brother and the son of a noble brother." He said: "Go, for you are the freed ones (al-Tulaqa')." And Ahmad and Abu Dawud related from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that "a man insulted Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and when he responded, the Prophet (ﷺ) stood (p-341) and then said: 'O Abu Bakr! Three things are all true: no servant is wronged by an injustice and then pardons it for the sake of Allah, except that Allah strengthens his support by it; and no man opens a door of giving, desiring thereby kinship, except that Allah increases him by it in abundance; and no man opens a door of asking, desiring thereby increase, except that Allah increases him by it in scarcity.'"

When this discourse made clear the matter of patience, which is limited to it, that gathers forgiveness toward it, and that requires victory, He placed all of them within the circle of truth. He followed this with those who went outside that circle. He said, informing that what He willed came to be and what He did not will did not come to be, as a conjunction to something like: ﴿Whomever Allah guides to stand at these limits, for him there is no misleader.﴾ By the expression of misguidance, He made clear that the path He prescribed is in the utmost clarity, and no one swerves from it except by a great expulsion: ﴿And whomever Allah misguides﴾, that is, He whose attributes are perfect, with a manifest misguidance, by what the disjunction implies through the absence of clarification, or through the absence of success in patience in general, whether the restraint is in taking the right, or in delaying the right until a time, or in pardoning, or in forgiving.

Since the one who strays from this can only be one disposed to evil, He made the following statement its consequence: ﴿Then he has no﴾, that is, at that time, ﴿protector﴾, that is, one who takes charge of his matter in guidance by clarifying what Allah has concealed from him, or by granting success in what He has made clear to him, ﴿after Him﴾, that is, after Allah's treatment of him as one far away, who has left him to himself and to others among creation, for any part of the time of distance, even if it is brief. (p-342)

Since the foundation of the matter of the misguided is regret, even after a while, He said, conjoining to something like: ﴿Then you see the wrongdoers﴾, before seeing the punishment, in the utmost arrogance, insolence, and denial of the power over them; therefore they do not hope for a reckoning and do not fear punishment. He said ﴿And you see﴾ and said ﴿the wrongdoers﴾ in place of "and you see them," to make clear that the misguided one does not place anything in its proper place. Since their punishment is certain, He expressed it in the past tense, saying: ﴿When they see the punishment﴾, that is, the known end of the wrongdoer, with a comprehensive sight encompassing its outside and inside, they wish for a return to the world to make up for what has passed of the acts of obedience that bring about salvation. ﴿They say﴾, that is, repeatedly, from the bewilderment that has seized them and the fear that has overpowered their hearts: ﴿Is there any way of return﴾, that is, a return to the abode of action and its time, which would deliver them from this punishment? ﴿from some way﴾

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 45:

When he had established their seeing the punishment, he established their being brought near to its place, and the state they are in during that nearness. So He said: ﴿And you will see them﴾, that is, O most perfect of creation, and O you who longs (p-343) to know their condition with your own eye, ﴿being exposed﴾, that is, He renews their exposure and repeats it, which is their being compelled to be brought near it, so that they may compare it with their exposure, which necessarily requires their being aligned with it, also in their full length, so that they know that it is their destination and that there is no escape from it for them. ﴿To it﴾, that is, to the Fire, which is the abode of punishment, repeatedly exposed throughout the length of the standing, together with what they are in of those terrors, enduring what is upon them of heavy burdens, ﴿humbled﴾, that is, in the utmost lowliness and casting down of the hand, a humility that is fixed for them.

Since humility may be praiseworthy, He said: ﴿from abasement﴾, because at that time they came to know their sins, and the greatness of the One they disobeyed was revealed to them.

Since abasement takes many forms, He depicted it in its most ugly form, and said, expressing it with the word "looking," which is the touching of sight to the outward form of what is seen: ﴿they look﴾, that is, they begin their repeated looking ﴿from a glance﴾, that is, a movement of the eyelids ﴿hidden﴾, through which the abasement is recognized, for because of not gazing directly, one hardly thinks that they blink, since they steal glances stealthily, just as you see a person looking at what he dislikes, and the patient one looks (p-344) at the sword that has been drawn against him, so he is in a state where he does not fix his gaze on what he looks at, rather he may imagine it greater than it is. When He depicted their condition, and since the most dreadful and heart-cutting of things is the gloating of the enemy, He said, giving good news to all kinds of the people of faith and warning the people of disbelief: ﴿And those who believed will say﴾, that is, in that greatest standing, by way of addressing them, rebuking, reproaching and censuring them, ﴿those who believed﴾, that is, those who realized this truth, whether their realization of it was at the lowest or the highest rank, upon seeing them in this state, emphasizing their statement to establish it before the One who decreed their misguidance, and informing of the joy they have in the good state of their own, and praise belongs to the One who favored them with awareness of their final outcome and end. It is also possible that this statement of theirs is in this world, because of the awe that overcame their hearts when they realized these admonitions: ﴿Indeed, the losers﴾, that is, those whose loss is complete, they alone, ﴿are those who have lost themselves﴾ through what the punishment has engulfed them in, ﴿and their families﴾ by being separated from them, either in the enclosing punishment if they were like them in loss, or in the abode of reward if they were among the people of faith. (p-345) When He informed of their loss, He placed a time-frame around it to magnify it. It is also possible that it is a time-frame for this statement, and it is more deterring for one who has any sense, because whoever allows that he might lose, and that his enemy will witness his loss and display gloating over him, would be deserving of abandoning the cause that leads to loss. So He said: ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is, the day in which there is no possibility of making amends, because it is for recompense, not for works, since the condition of works has failed with the failure of belief in the unseen, due to the lifting of the veil. When this was the extreme of loss, it produced His saying, calling out and mentioning the cause of this specific loss, emphasized in order to deny the wrongdoers its reality, even though it is part of the statement of the believers there. So the emphasis, together with what the information conveys in this world, serves to deter the one who denies, and to inform of the pleasure they have in what they saw of the evil of their state, the rending of their limbs, and their despair that this would cease for them, as it ceases for the sinful among the believers: ﴿Unquestionably, the wrongdoers﴾, that is, those firmly rooted in this description, such that they do not cease from the act of one who walks in darkness, placing things in other than their places, ﴿are in an enduring punishment﴾ that never departs from them at all. Therefore they are never relieved of it at any time, and for this reason their loss is total in every respect.

Since it is the custom that whoever falls into a predicament usually finds either a helper to support him or a way to deliver him, he said, as a conjunction to ﴿And you see them﴾ [al-Shura: 45], or to "Verily" ("ألا إنَّ"): ﴿And they had not﴾, meaning it was not valid and did not obtain, ﴿for them﴾, and he intensified the negation, saying: ﴿any protectors﴾, so they have no protector at all, because if help is negated from the group, it is negated from the individual a fortiori.

Since one who performs the act of a near kinsman benefits only if he is able to give help, he said: ﴿who would help them﴾, meaning that their help would be found at some time, neither in this world, by being able to rescue them from the attribute of wrongdoing, nor in the Hereafter, by rescuing them from the punishment that befell them. Since God, exalted is He, may do whatever He wills, directly or through intermediaries or otherwise, he said: ﴿besides Allah﴾, meaning that such help is not valid or possible in any way apart from Him. As for Him, it is valid for Him and possible for Him, because He encompasses the attributes of perfection, and were He to will, He would do it.

Having stated what belongs to them, he then stated what belongs to whoever is characterized by their attribute, whoever he may be, saying, based on the fact that it is He who led them astray: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray﴾, meaning that his straying is brought into existence with thorough effectiveness, by what the withholding of guidance has produced, continuously, through not being made clear to him, or through not being granted success after clarification: ﴿then there is not for him﴾, because of his being led astray, ﴿any means﴾, meaning any deliverance from error or from the punishment that results from it. He intensified the negation with his saying ﴿any way﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 47:

When this was the case (p-347), it produced, decisively, His saying: ﴿Respond﴾, that is, seek the response and bring it into being, and he turned the speech to the attribute of bounty, as a reminder of what urges toward harmony and shames one out of discord and dissension, so He said: ﴿to your Lord﴾, who, in what He has called you to through His Messenger ﷺ, has shown you no bounty except that it comes from Him, of fulfilling His covenant in His commands and prohibitions. Do not be among those who abandon that, lest you be among those who know that He has led them astray, so that the way is closed to them.

When fear of missing the opportunity necessitates haste, He said, indicating with the prepositional phrase that any small good is counted, if it occurs in the briefest time before death: ﴿before there comes a Day﴾, that is, a day in which no salvation is possible. Then He described it by His saying, pointing to the Greatest Name, which comprises the attributes of bounty and beneficence toward the obedient and of domination and retribution against the disobedient: ﴿there is no turning back﴾, that is, no averting, no place for averting, and no time for averting, ﴿for it﴾ existing ﴿from Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom belongs all greatness. If there is no averting of it from Him, there is no averting of it from anyone else. And when that is absent, it produced His saying: ﴿you will have no refuge﴾, and He intensified the negation by His saying: ﴿on that Day﴾, that is, no place to which you may take refuge on that day and no fortress in which you may shelter from anything you dislike. He increased the emphasis by repeating the negation and what falls within its scope, as an intensification in warning, so He said: ﴿nor will you have any denial﴾ (p-348), that is, any denial by which you might be enabled to be saved, because the guardian angels bear witness against you; if you are truthful to them, well and good, otherwise your limbs and your skins will testify against you. Nor will you have anyone who denies anything of what you are overtaken by, so as to deliver you from it.

When he had finished what he had presented in His words, ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion﴾ [al-Shura: 13], its conclusion, and had indicated it and everything that wisdom leads to within its scope, until no one retained any doubt about anything, that was a reason for warning them against turning away from it and for consoling his Messenger (ﷺ). So He said, turning away from addressing them, as a declaration of intense anger: ﴿But if they turn away﴾, that is, from answering this call, which must be answered, and from the Law whose path has been made clear and sound through the proofs by which it was confirmed. He turned the speech toward the manifestation of greatness to repel what might suggest that sending was out of need, and said: ﴿We have not sent you﴾, despite what We possess of greatness, ﴿as a guardian over them﴾, that is, We will not compel them to comply with what We have sent you with. Since the implied sense was: "So he turned away from anything other than conveying to them, because We only sent you as a conveyer," the words ﴿But﴾, meaning "only," were placed in its position: ﴿upon you is only the conveying﴾ of what We have sent you with. As for guidance and misguidance, they rest with Us.

When He had secured for this verse what He had sent him with, He followed it with what man is created upon, as an explanation, because he (ﷺ) has no authority over natural dispositions, and what is incumbent upon him is only to make them hear, not to make them listen. So He said, connecting it to what precedes the verse of the Law, from His words ﴿He extends provision for whom He wills﴾ [al-Shura: 12], speaking of it in the style of greatness, as an alert that He is the One who judged against them with turning away from what is worthy of not being turned away from by any sensible person. It also hints that man, because of his overwhelming ignorance and scant intellect, becomes bold with the slightest familiarity toward the One before whose greatness mountains are made to dissolve and lofty peaks crumble from awe of Him: ﴿And when We let them taste﴾ by Our greatness, which cannot be opposed. Since the one who rejoices in a blessing when he alone possesses it is blameworthy, He expressed it with a collective noun suitable for one or more, as an alert that the nature of man is not to concern himself with the hardships of his brothers, except for one whom God has placed in the station of goodness. So He said: ﴿man﴾, that is, with what We have created him with of deficiency: haste and lack of self-restraint, ﴿from Us a mercy﴾, that is, a kind of honor, such as health, (p-350) or wealth, or the like. He used the singular pronoun to indicate that he is disposed to think that nothing is due except from himself, even if all the people of the earth were otherwise. Likewise He expressed it with ﴿man﴾ and said: ﴿he rejoices in it﴾, that is, even if all the people of the earth were in affliction, misery, and blindness, the joy takes him away from reflecting on what benefits him so that he may give thanks. Thus, because of that, he becomes ungrateful for the blessing, since he has replaced gratitude with joy, and disbelief, and so he reaches disobedience through well-being, and thereby places himself in the greatest of trials.

When He indicated, by the particle of certainty, that blessing is the primary element because of the generality of His mercy, and that it precedes His wrath, He indicated, by the particle of doubt and the present tense, that evil is few in comparison to it, and said: ﴿But if﴾. Since sharing hardships lightens calamities, and whoever increases his grief by the particular of his own calamity during a general affliction is blameworthy, He alerted to the deficiency of man in this respect by using the plural, and said: ﴿an evil befalls them﴾, that is, a punishment, trial, or hardship. Since mercy is a bounty from Him, He informed them that the evil results from them, and said: ﴿because of what their hands have sent forward﴾. He expressed the whole by "hands," because most action is done with them. Since the response was according to the pattern of the first (that is, "they rejoice"), He changed it to what indicates that the nature of man is a locus of ingratitude: "they despair and disbelieve." (p-351) Since they claimed to be thankful and denied ungratefulness, He emphasized His statement and attributed to that affliction and tasting together, to indicate that there is no origin for it other than these two. So He said, placing the explicit noun in the position of the pronoun so as to state the judgment upon the species as such: ﴿Indeed, man﴾, that is, the one who is at ease with himself and turns away from others by what is his nature, because of touching him with harm, ﴿is ungrateful﴾, that is, extremely concealing of blessings and forgetful of them. He forgets, at the first shock of affliction, all the blessings that preceded it, and knows only the present state. If he is in blessings, he is insolent and boastful; if he is in afflictions, he despairs and is hopeless. This is the condition of the species as such. Whoever God grants success is spared this, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The believer, if good befalls him, gives thanks, and that is good for him; and if harm befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him." And this is only for the believer. The verse is of the rhetorical device of al-ihtibak (mutual omission): mention of joy first indicates the sorrow second, and mention of ingratitude second indicates its omission first.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 49:

ولَمّا قَدَّمَ سُبْحانَهُ في هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ أنَّ لَهُ التَّصَرُّفَ التّامَّ في عالَمِ (p-٣٥٢)الخَلْقِ بِالأجْسامِ المَرْئِيَّةِ وفي عالِمِ الأمْرِ بِالأرْواحِ الحِسِّيَّةِ والمَعْنَوِيَّةِ القائِمَةِ بِالأبْدانِ والمُدَبِّرَةِ لِلْأدْيانِ، وغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِن بَدِيعِ الشَّأْنِ، فَقالَ في افْتِتاحِ السُّورَةِ ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُوحِي إلَيْكَ وإلى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾ [الشورى: ٣] وأتْبَعَهُ أشْكالَهُ إلى أنْ قالَ ﴿أمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرى عَلى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا فَإنْ يَشَأِ اللَّهُ يَخْتِمْ عَلى قَلْبِكَ﴾ [الشورى: ٢٤] الآيَةُ ﴿فاطِرُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ جَعَلَ لَكم مِن أنْفُسِكم أزْواجًا ومِنَ الأنْعامِ أزْواجًا﴾ [الشورى: ١١] - الآيَةُ ﴿لَهُ مَقالِيدُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ [الشورى: ١٢] ﴿اللَّهُ لَطِيفٌ بِعِبادِهِ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشاءُ﴾ [الشورى: ١٩] ﴿مَن كانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الآخِرَةِ﴾ [الشورى: ٢٠] - الآيَةُ،

﴿ولَوْ بَسَطَ اللَّهُ الرِّزْقَ لِعِبادِهِ لَبَغَوْا في الأرْضِ﴾ [الشورى: ٢٧] ﴿ومِن آياتِهِ الجَوارِ في البَحْرِ كالأعْلامِ﴾ [الشورى: ٣٢] - الآيَةُ إلى أنْ ذَكَرَ أحْوالَ الآخِرَةِ في قَوْلِهِ ﴿وتَرى الظّالِمِينَ لَمّا رَأوُا العَذابَ يَقُولُونَ﴾ [الشورى: ٤٤] - الآياتُ، وخَتَمَ بِتَصَرُّفِهِ المُطْلَقِ في الإنْسانِ مِن إنْعامٍ وانْتِقامٍ، وما لَهُ مِنَ الطَّبْعِ المُعْوَجِّ مَعَ ما وهَبَهُ لَهُ مِنَ العَقْلِ المُقَيَّمِ في أحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ، فَدَلَّ ذَلِكَ عَلى أنَّ لَهُ التَّصَرُّفَ التّامَّ مُلْكًا ومَلَكُوتًا خَلْقًا وأمْرًا، أتْبَعُهُ الدَّلِيلُ عَلى أنَّ تَصَرُّفَهُ ذَلِكَ عَلى سَبِيلِ المُلْكِ والقَهْرَ إيجادًا وإعْدامًا إهانَةً وإكْرامًا، فَقالَ صارِفًا القَوْلَ عَنْ أُسْلُوبِ العَظَمَةِ الَّتِي (p-٣٥٣)مِن حَقِّها دَوامُ الخُضُوعِ وإهْلاكِ الجَبابِرَةِ إلى أعْظَمَ مِنها بِذِكْرِ الِاسْمِ الأعْظَمِ الجامِعِ لِمَظْهَرِ العَظَمَةِ ومَقامِ اللُّطْفِ والإحْسانِ والرَّحْمَةِ نَتِيجَةً لِكُلِّ ما مَضى: ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ أيِ المَلِكِ الأعْظَمِ وحْدَهُ لا شَرِيكَ لَهُ ﴿مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ﴾ كُلُّها عَلى عُلُوِّها وارْتِفاعِها وتَطابُقِها وكِبَرِها وعِظَمِها وتَباعُدِ أقْطارِها ﴿والأرْضِ﴾ جَمِيعُها عَلى تَبايُنِها وتَكاثُفِها واخْتِلافُ أقْطارِها وسُكّانِها واتِّساعِها.

ولَمّا أخْبَرَ بِانْفِرادِهِ بِالمُلْكِ، دَلَّ عَلَيْهِ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿يَخْلُقُ﴾ أيْ عَلى سَبِيلِ التَّجَدُّدِ والِاسْتِمْرارِ ﴿ما يَشاءُ﴾ أيْ وإنْ كانَ عَلى غَيْرِ اخْتِيارِ العِبادِ، ثُمَّ دَلَّ عَلى ذَلِكَ بِما يُشاهِدُ مِن حالِ النّاسِ فَإنَّهُ لِما اسْتَوى البَشَرُ في الإنْسانِيَّةِ والنِّكاحِ الَّذِي هو سَبَبُ الوِلادَةِ اخْتَلَفَتْ أصْنافُ أوْلادِهِمْ. كانَ ذَلِكَ أدَلُّ دَلِيلٍ عَلى أنَّهُ لا اخْتِيارَ لِأحَدٍ مَعَهُ وأنَّ الأسْبابَ لا تُؤَثِّرُ أصْلًا إلّا بِهِ. ولَمّا كانَتْ وِلادَةُ الإناثِ أدَلُّ عَلى عَدَمِ اخْتِيارِ الوَلَدِ وكانُوا يَعُدُّونَهُ مِنَ البَلاءِ الَّذِي خَتَمَ بِهِ ما قَبْلَها قَدَّمَهُنَّ في الذِّكْرِ فَقالَ: ﴿يَهَبُ﴾ خَلْقًا ومَوْلِدًا ﴿لِمَن يَشاءُ﴾ أوْلادًا (p-٣٥٤)﴿إناثًا﴾ أيْ فَقَطْ لَيْسَ مَعَهُنَّ ذِكْرٌ كَما في لُوطٍ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ، وعَبَّرَ سُبْحانَهُ فِيهِنَّ بِلَفْظِ الهِبَةِ لِأنَّ الأوْهامَ العادِيَّةَ قَدْ تَكْتَنِفُ العَقْلَ فَتَحْجُبُهُ عَنْ تَأمُّلِ مَحاسِنِ التَّدْبِيراتِ الإلَهِيَّةِ، وتَرْمِي بِهِ في مُهاوِي الأسْبابِ الدُّنْيَوِيَّةِ، فَيَقَعُ المُسْلِمُ مَعَ إسْلامِهِ في مُضاهاةِ الكُفّارِ في كَراهَةِ البَناتِ وفي وادِي الوَأْدِ بِتَضْيِيعِهِنَّ أوِ التَّقْصِيرِ في حُقُوقِهِنَّ وتَنْبِيهًا عَلى أنَّ الأُنْثى نِعْمَةٌ، وأنَّ نِعْمَتَها لا تَنْقُصُ عَنْ نِعْمَةِ الذَّكَرِ ورُبَّما زادَتْ، وإيقاظًا مِن سِنَةِ الغَفْلَةِ عَلى أنَّ التَّقْدِيمَ وإنْ كانَ لِما قَدَّمَتْهُ لا يُقَدِّمُ تَأْنِيسًا وتَوْصِيَةً لَهُنَّ واهْتِمامًا بِأمْرِهِنَّ، نَقَلَ ابْنُ مَيْلَقٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَطِيَّةَ عَنِ الثَّعْلَبِيِّ أنَّ واثِلَةَ بْنَ الأسْقَعِ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قالَ: مَن يُمْنِ المَرْأةِ تَبْكِيرُها بِالأُنْثى قَبْلَ الذَّكَرِ لِأنَّ اللهَ تَعالى بَدَأ بِالإناثِ، ولِذَلِكَ رَغَّبَ النَّبِيُّ صَلّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وسَلَّمَ في الإحْسانِ إلَيْهِنَّ في أحادِيثَ كَثِيرَةٍ ورَتَّبَ عَلى ذَلِكَ أجَرًا كَبِيرًا ولِأجْلِ تَضْمِينِ الهِبَةِ مَعَ الخَلْقِ عَداها بِاللّامِ مَعَ أنَّ فِعْلَها مُتَعَدٍّ بِنَفْسِهِ إلى مَفْعُولَيْنِ لِئَلّا يَتَوَهَّمَ أنَّ الوَلَدَ كانَ لِغَيْرِ الوالِدِ ووَهَبَهُ اللهُ لَهُ. (p-٣٥٥)ولَمّا كانَ الذَّكَرُ حاضِرًا في الذِّهْنِ لِشَرَفِهِ ومَيْلِ النَّفْسِ إلَيْهِ لا سِيَّما وقَدْ ذَكَرَ بِهِ ذِكْرَ الإناثِ، عَرَّفَ لِذَلِكَ وجَبْرًا لِما فَوَّتَهُ مِنَ التَّقْدِيمِ في الذَّكَرِ تَنْبِيهًا عَلى أنَّهُ ما أخَّرَ إلّا لَمّا ذَكَرَ مِنَ المَعْنى فَقالَ: ﴿ويَهَبُ لِمَن يَشاءُ الذُّكُورَ﴾ أيْ فَقَطْ لَيْسَ بَيْنَهُنَّ أُنْثى كَما صَنَعَ لِإبْراهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ وهو عَمُّ لُوطٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ.

When he had finished with the first two divisions, he followed them with a third that pairs with them, and he indicated, by using "or" (aw), that he was dividing. He said: ﴿Or He couples them, males and females,﴾ meaning the children, by making them pairs, that is, two kinds, ﴿males and females﴾, either gathered together in one womb or separated, just as He bestowed on Muhammad (ﷺ). He ordered these two here according to the original arrangement, as a reminder that He did not act otherwise in the past except for sublime wisdoms, which must therefore be sought out. He expressed the males with the form that is more emphatic in multiplicity, to encourage asking Him and submitting humbly before Him in hope of His bounty.

When he had finished with the three categories of those granted gifts, he followed the bestowal of favour with the negation of that, saying, in the place where one would say, for example: "He does not grant any of that to whom He wills." ﴿And He makes whom He wills barren﴾, meaning he does not have children, like Yahya ibn Zakariyya, peace be upon them both. This is what they have said, but the apparent view is that it is not valid as an example, since he did not marry. Ibn Maylaq said: the root of 'aqim (barren) is dryness that prevents receptiveness to influence in what ought to be influenced, and the disease 'iqam is the one that does not accept cure. End of quote. What he mentioned is clearer in meaning because of the mention of barrenness, and more indicative of power, since it includes the one who has the capacity for intercourse and emission, lest one think that the absence of offspring is due to not pursuing its causes. They also mentioned Jesus, peace be upon him, in this category, but this is not valid, because it is reported that he will marry after his descent and will have children. This fourfold division in the roots is like the fourfold division in the branches: some have neither males nor females, like Adam, peace be upon him; some have only males, like Hawwa' (Eve), peace be upon her; some have only females, like Jesus, peace be upon him; and some have both males and females, which is the case for most people. Thus the indication is complete that what He wills comes to be, and none can repel it; and what He does not will does not come to be. There is no creator of it, no preventer of what He gives, and no giver of what He withholds.

When this evidential demonstration, which is witnessed, has shown what the verse was built upon, namely the affirmation of dominion for Him alone, together with what it added of the nature of the context, the sweetness of its words, the firmness of its doubt-removal, and the inimitable arrangement and composition, the conclusion was given as a definitive matter, since their associating others with Him implies a challenge to His unique dominion, placing first the attribute that is the greatest of the conditions of dominion: ﴿Indeed, He is All-Knowing﴾, meaning of utmost knowledge of the interests of the servants and other matters, ﴿All-Powerful﴾, whose power encompasses the creation of whatever He wills.

When the first division, concerning what He built upon knowledge and power, was complete, in which power is more evident, in agreement with what the verse was concluded with, and since His creating a thing may be an origination without any intermediate cause, and may be through an intermediate cause, He followed it with the other, higher division, in which knowledge is more evident. This is revelation, whose verse was concluded at the beginning of the surah with wisdom, which is the secret of knowledge. Its division is likewise into what is through an intermediary and what is without one. But the secret of the implied element (*taqdir*) in the first division is speech, the faculty by which man was honored, and no one could speak except through God's speaking to him, that is, His bringing speech into being in his heart. He said: ﴿And it is not for a human﴾, that is, while He, glorified be He, is perfect in knowledge and all-encompassing in power, having implanted in human beings the instinct of knowledge and enabled them by His power to articulate it, by way of revelation from Him to him, as He revealed to the bee and the like. The state is that it is not [possible] for a human, among the aforementioned divisions, and He resolved the verbal noun, which is the subject of *kāna* (the subject of "was"), so that the agent and the object would be stated in their fullest form. So He said: ﴿that Allah should speak to him﴾ [p. 358], and He placed the explicit name in the position of the pronoun, to magnify revelation and to honor its rank by the majesty of its being chosen. So He said: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, who combines all attributes of perfection, is found speaking in his heart, ﴿except by revelation﴾, that is, a hidden speech which He brings into being within him without an intermediary, in a concealed manner that no one perceives except through a departure from the ordinary course, whether by inspiration, or by a dream vision, or otherwise. Whether Allah creates in the one addressed the capacity to hear it, which is the most noble of these divisions absolutely, whether that is together with seeing, so that it is a counterpart to what follows it, or first, or He creates that capacity in him, is immaterial. From this final division are: ﴿And We revealed to the mother of Moses﴾ [al-Qasas: 7], ﴿And your Lord revealed to the bee﴾ [al-Nahl: 68], and ﴿And He revealed in each heaven its affair﴾ [Fussilat: 12], for placing in them the faculties by which benefits are obtained is like placing in a human the faculty of speech, then the faculty of expressing it. And Allah knows best. This is the meaning of the words of Qadi 'Iyad in *al-Shifa'*, at the end of the second section of the fourth chapter on inimitability: "It has been said concerning His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And it is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation﴾, the verse, that it means what He casts into his heart without an intermediary." And the meaning of the words of the Imam Shihab al-Din al-Suhrawardi in the twenty-sixth chapter of his *'Awarif al-Ma'arif*: "And the knowledge of the divine gift [p. 359] in the hearts of those devoted to Allah is a kind of divine discourse."

Since the physical veil conceals what is behind it from sight, the term was borrowed for hiddenness in general. So He said: ﴿Or from behind a veil﴾, that is, speech existing without an intermediary, yet with hearing the very speech of Allah, whose owner is existing from a manner in which the speaker is not seen, along with hearing the speech in an audible manner. Al-Qushayri said: "The one veiled is the servant, not the Lord. The veil is that He creates in the locus of sight something opposite to sight. Allah is exalted above being behind a veil, because that is a property of bodies." End of quotation.

The verse can be interpreted by *ihtibak* (a rhetorical device in which each of two elements omits what the other supplies): the mention of the veil second is evidence of its negation first, and the mention of revelation, which indicates concealment, first is evidence of audibility second, and the veil second is evidence of seeing first. Its secret is that abstaining from explicit statement and from indicating seeing by the veil is more appropriate to the context of majesty.

Since what occurs without an intermediary, despite being the most hidden of the divisions, contains no sound and is not arranged in words, He expressed it with the verbal noun, and expressed what the angel conveys with what indicates renewal, so He said: ﴿Or sends﴾, which is coordinated with the verbal noun after resolving it, ﴿a messenger﴾, that is, from among the angels. Since revelation is caused by sending and follows it, He said: ﴿so he reveals﴾ [p. 360], that is, in a manner of renewal and sequence. Nafi' read *yursilu* and *yuhi* with a nominative ending, on the estimate: "or He Himself sends." Since one might suppose that the intermediary has an act of its own separate from His act, He refuted that with His saying: ﴿by His permission﴾, that is, by His enabling and empowering. So that conveyor is merely an instrument. Since His messenger does not depart from what He has determined for him in any respect, He said: ﴿what He wills﴾, that is, he does not exceed His intent and enablement at all. So He is the true speaker. It has become clear that these are three divisions: the first contains two divisions, and the first of them, in both its parts, is specified by explicit mention of the name of revelation, because, as already noted, it is the most hidden, and it also occurs instantaneously, and the meaning of revelation revolves around hiddenness and speed.

Since the divisions indicate a dazzling majesty, and since they belong to the bodily spirit, for the spirit of revelation grants the bodily spirit the life of knowledge, just as the spirit gives the body the life of movement through will and sensation, the conclusion was made to confirm that their slander of the Messenger, the Qur'an, and monotheism includes their slander of the content of the sentence: ﴿Indeed He﴾, that is, the One who has this great disposition over this noble revelation, ﴿is Most High﴾, that is, He reaches the utmost degree of exaltedness above what is unfitting for Him of attributes, and above what the creatures' lowness in regard to His majesty entails, through the veils that are upon them. So nothing of what is expressed [p. 361] in order to bring things closer to minds is confused with what would suggest deficiency, for figurative usage is well known in the language of the Arabs. ﴿Wise﴾, who perfects what He does with a perfection that minds cannot fully grasp. So the spirit of knowledge, which is among the subtlest of His secrets, dwells in the bodily spirit that governs it, so that it is a secret within a secret, just as it was righteousness after righteousness. He makes that sometimes through an intermediary and sometimes without one, according to what the situation requires, and expresses every meaning by what its context requires. Whenever something of that appears to suggest a deficiency, the discerning person returns it to the clear (muhkam) by some kind of interpretation, according to what the common usage requires, and returns in a manifest and perfected way, to the point that it becomes most evident.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 42, verse 52 (part 1 of 2):

Since revelation is a spirit that governs the spirit, just as the spirit governs the body, he stated this explicitly, saying: ﴿And thus﴾, meaning: and in the same way as We have informed you of the manners in which We reveal to Our servants, ﴿We have revealed to you﴾, turning the speech to the place of manifestation of greatness, to magnify what was revealed to him and the blessings He bestowed upon him in all those categories. So the speech turned [from the third person to the first person] in the matter of the spirit, being mentioned and not unknown. Hearing without a veil is transmitted in reports about the night of the Mi'raj (Night Journey and Ascension), and it is rationally understood to be hearing from behind a veil as well, in which He mentioned in His words: "I have decreed My obligation and lightened it for My servants." Revelation through an angel is very frequent. He magnified revelation and ennobled it by describing it with an indefinite form, for magnification, reverence and honour, in His words for the spirit that is with Him, the spirit of command, to convey that this Book, which left the eloquent speechless, rendered the rhetoricians incapable, and bewildered the minds of the wise, is a branch of it and a particle emerging from it. It is also possible that the indefinite form ﴿a spirit﴾ is for magnification, reverence and honour: whoever mingles with it, his heart becomes alive, and whoever is stripped of it, his heart is dead. Its greatness increased with His words: ﴿from Our command﴾, meaning: by making it part of the category of command and manifesting it in the place of greatness. How lofty this is, before which every high thing shrinks and before whose grandeur every praiser belittles himself. The purpose of this is to refute what was previously mentioned, when you attributed to him (ﷺ) [the claim of] fabrication, because He, the Exalted, did not seal his heart but opened it with the hand of power and gave it life with the spirit of revelation, so He caused him to speak the wisdoms before which the wise submitted and before whose depth the minds of scholars admitted incapacity. He indicated this by His words, negating and clarifying his state (ﷺ) before this revelation: ﴿You did not know﴾, meaning: during the forty years that passed for you while you were among your people, equal to them in that you knew nothing and did not utter anything of that. This is the meaning of ﴿you knew﴾. He expressed it with the interrogative particle to indicate that what follows it must be given attention and asked about. He attached the knowing about action to the interrogative clause, and it took the place of the two objects of knowing: ﴿what the Book is﴾, meaning (p. 363) it was not in your nature to know this with even the lowest kind of knowledge, neither through disputation nor otherwise; ﴿nor the faith﴾, meaning: the detailed legislation as We have defined it for you through what We have revealed to you. He (ﷺ), although before prophethood he affirmed the oneness and greatness of Allah, the Exalted, did not know the prophets as they were. There is no doubt that testifying to his own prophethood (ﷺ) is part of the pillars of faith, and he had no knowledge of this; likewise the angels and the Last Day. Thus it is sound to negate what is negated because its whole is missing.

Since the meaning is: "But We have made you know all of that," He expressed it this way to inform that the creation was in darkness, because they used to act by placing things in other than their proper places, like one who walks in darkness, saying: ﴿But We have made it﴾, meaning the spirit, which is the Book sent down from Us to you, the teacher of faith and every recognition by what We possess of greatness, ﴿a light by which We guide﴾ according to Our greatness, ﴿whomever We will﴾, specifically, no one can be guided by it without Our will, ﴿of Our servants﴾, by creating guidance in his heart. Ibn Burjan said: whoever is granted the criterion (furqan) that distinguishes between ambiguous matters, and the light by which he walks in darkness, that is the one who has seen the ray of light and witnessed the radiance spread throughout the created world. In proportion to his turning toward it and his freedom from every preoccupation other than it, is his acceptance of it and his guidance by it. Al-Isfahani said, in the commentary on Surat al-Nur: it is the quality that flows from the sun, the moon, and fire, for example, onto the earth, the wall and other things; one says, "the earth became illuminated." Hujjat al-Islam al-Ghazali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: It is well known that this quality is singled out for excellence and honour, because visible things become manifest through it. Then it is well known that just as the perception of these visible things depends on their being illuminated, so it also depends on the existence of the seeing eye, which is the perceiver, and by which perception occurs. Thus the attribute of manifestation through seeing light is more deserving of the name "light" than the seeing light itself. For this reason, they applied the name "light" to the light of the seeing eye, and they said of the bat that the light of its eyes is weak, and of the blind that he has lost the light of sight. Having established this, we say: a human has sight (basar) and insight (basira). Sight is the visible eye that perceives lights and colours, and insight is the rational faculty. Each of the two kinds of perception requires light, and the light of the intellect is stronger and more intense than the light of the eye, because the faculty of sight does not perceive itself, nor its perception, nor its instruments, whereas the rational faculty perceives itself, its perception, and its instruments. So the light of the intellect is more perfect than the light of sight. The rational faculty perceives universals, and the faculty of sight does not perceive them; and the perception of universals is more noble than the perception of particulars, because it does not change, unlike particulars. The perception of the intellect is productive, and the perception of particulars is not productive. The faculty of sight perceives only the outer surface of a body and the colour existing on that surface, with the condition of light. When it perceives a human, it perceives only the outer surface of his body and the colour existing on it. The rational faculty perceives the outer and inner aspects of things, for the inner and outer are equal in relation to it. So the rational faculty is light in relation to the outer and inner, while the faculty of sight is darkness in relation to the inner. The object perceived by the rational faculty is Allah, His attributes and His acts, while the object perceived by the faculty of sight is colours and shapes. Thus the ratio of the nobility of the rational faculty to the nobility of the faculty of sight is like the ratio of the nobility of the essence of Allah to the nobility of colours and shapes. The faculty of sight is like a servant and the rational faculty is like a ruler, and the ruler is more noble than the servant. The faculty of sight may err, but the rational faculty does not err. Thus it is established that rational perception is more perfect, more powerful and more noble than visual perception. Each of the two perceptions requires manifestation, which is the noblest property of light, so rational perception is more deserving of being called light. Rational perception is of two kinds: one is necessarily obtained when the faculties and instruments are sound, and these are the innate intellections; the other is acquired, and these are the speculative intellections. It is not among the necessary attributes of the essence of a human, because in childhood he knew nothing at all. These lights were acquired after they had not been present, so they must have a cause. The human nature may be subject to deviation, so there must be a guide and a director, and there is no guide above the words of Allah and His prophets. Thus the status of the verses of the Qur'an in the eye of the intellect is like the status of the light of the sun, just as the light of the sun is called light. So the light of the Qur'an resembles the light of the sun, and the light of the intellect resembles the light of the eye. By this, the meaning of His saying, the Exalted, becomes clear: ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the light which We have sent down﴾ [al-Taghabun: 8], ﴿There has come to you a proof from your Lord﴾ [al-Nisa': 174], ﴿And We have sent down to you a manifest light﴾ [al-Nisa': 174]. Since it is established that the explanation of the Messenger (ﷺ) is stronger than the light of the sun, it necessarily follows that his holy soul is greater in luminosity than the sun, just as the sun in the world of bodies gives light to others and does not receive it from others. Likewise the soul of the Prophet (ﷺ) gives rational lights to the rest of human souls and does not receive rational light from any human souls. Therefore Allah described the sun as a lamp, and described Muhammad (ﷺ) as a lamp. Then he said: The degrees of lights in (p. 367) the world of spirits have an example: when the light of the sun reaches the moon, then enters a window of a house and falls on a mirror set on a wall, then is reflected from it to a basin full of water placed on the ground, then is reflected from it to the ceiling of the house, the greatest light is in the sun, which is the source; the second is in the moon, the third in the mirror, the fourth in the water, and the fifth in the ceiling. Whatever is closer to the source is stronger. Likewise, the heavenly lights, since they are arranged in order, the light that gives is more brilliant. Then these lights continue to be arranged until they reach the greatest light, and the spirit, which is the greatest of spirits in rank with Allah, is what is meant by His saying: ﴿The day the spirit and the angels stand in rows﴾ [al-Naba': 38]. Then we say: these sensible lights, whether lower, like the lights of fires, or higher, like the lights of the heavens, are possible in their essences, and the possible in its essence does not deserve existence in its essence; rather its existence is from another. Non-existence is darkness, and existence is light. So everything other than Allah is dark in itself, illuminated by the illumination of Allah, the Exalted. Likewise all their knowledges and their existence derive from the existence of Allah, the Exalted, for the Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who manifested them (p. 368) through existence after they were in the darkness of non-existence, and poured upon them the lights of knowledge after they were in the darkness of ignorance. So nothing has manifestation except by His manifesting it. Light especially is the bestowal of manifestation, disclosure, and revelation. At this point it becomes clear that the absolute light is Allah, glory be to Him, and that applying the name "light" to other than Him is metaphorical. Everything other than Allah, considered in itself, is pure darkness, because insofar as it is possible, it is pure non-existence. Lights, if one looks at them in themselves, are darkness, because in themselves they are possibilities, and the possible in itself is non-existent, and the non-existent is dark. So light, if viewed as possible, is dark. But if one turns to them in terms of the fact that the Truth, glory be to Him, has poured upon them the light of existence, in this respect they become lights. Thus it is established that He, glory be to Him, is the Light, and everything else is not light. He attributed light to the two horizons in His saying: ﴿Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Nur: 35], because they are filled with rational lights and sensible lights. As for sensible lights, they are what we witness in the heavens of stars and others, and on the earth of rays spread over the surfaces of bodies, by which the various colours appear, and were it not for them (p. 369) colours would have no manifestation, indeed no existence. As for rational lights, the higher world is filled with them, and they are the substances of the angels, and the lower world is filled with them, and they are the vegetative, animal and human faculties. By the lower human light the order of the lower world appears, just as by the angelic light the order of the higher world appears. When you know this, you know that the whole world is filled with visible lights and inner rational lights. Then you know that lower things emanate from one another, and the emanation of light is from the lamp, and the lamp is the prophetic spirit. Then the holy lights are borrowed from the higher lights, as a lamp borrows from light, and the higher things borrow from one another, and between them there is an order in ends. Then their totality ascends to the Light of Lights, its source and first origin, and that is Allah alone, without partner. So all is His light. Then he said: Imam al-Ghazali said: It has become clear that the perceptible faculties are lights.

The human perceptive faculties are five in number. The first is the sensory faculty (al-quwwa al-hassasa), which receives what the five senses convey. It is, as it were, the root of the animal spirit, for by it the animal becomes an animal. It is present in the infant and the suckling. The second is the imaginative faculty (al-quwwa al-khayaliyya), which retains what the senses have conveyed and keeps it stored with it, so that it is available to the intellectual faculty when there is need of it. The third is the intellectual faculty (al-quwwa al-'aqliyya), which perceives the universal realities. The fourth is the discursive faculty (al-quwwa al-fikriyya), which takes the intellectual cognitions and arranges them in a composition from which it derives knowledge of the unknown. The fifth is the holy faculty (al-quwwa al-qudsiyya), which is peculiar to the prophets and some of the saints, and in which the lights of the unseen and the secrets of the divine kingdom (malakut) become manifest. To this point His saying refers: ﴿And thus We revealed to you a spirit from Our command﴾, the verse. When you know these faculties, they are altogether lights, for through them the kinds of existent things appear. These five levels can be compared with the five matters that God mentioned in the niche, the glass, the lamp, the tree and the oil. As for the sensory spirit, if you consider its特性 you will find its lights issuing from openings such as the two eyes, the two ears and the two nostrils. So the gentlest example of it from the world of bodies is the niche (mishkah). As for the second, the imaginative spirit, it has three properties. The first is that it is of the substance of the lower, dense world, because the imagined thing has a shape and a place, and it is in the nature of bodily attachments to veil one from the purely intellectual lights. The second is that this dense imagination, when it becomes clear and refined, becomes a counterpart to the intellectual cognitions and conveys their lights; for this reason the interpreter of dreams (al-mu'abbir) infers intellectual meanings from imaginal forms, just as one infers sovereignty from the sun, a vizier from the moon, and, before dawn, the sealing of people's private parts and mouths as (a sign of) their ears. The third is that imagination, at the beginning, is needed so that by it one holds the intellectual cognitions fast and they do not become disordered. You will find nothing among bodies resembling imagination in these qualities except the glass, for it is in origin of a dense substance, but it became clear and refined until it no longer veils the light of the lamp but conveys it in its true form, and then it preserves it from being extinguished by means of the glass. As for the third, which is the intellectual faculty strong enough to perceive the universal quiddities and the divine cognitions, the reason for its being likened to the lamp is not hidden from you. As for the fourth, which is the discursive faculty, one of its properties is that it takes a single quiddity and then divides it into two parts, as when we say: the existent is either necessary or contingent; then it makes each part into two, and so on, until it reaches what admits no division; then at last it arrives at conclusions which are its fruit. It is therefore fitting that its example from this world be the tree. And since its fruits are the material for the increase and clarification of the lights of cognitions, it is fitting that it not be likened to the quince or apple tree, but specifically to the olive tree, because the essence of its fruit is the oil, which is the material of lamps, and it has, among all other fats, the special property of greater brightness and less smoke. And if the cattle whose milk and offspring are abundant, and the tree whose fruit is abundant, are called blessed, then that whose benefit and fruit have no end is more worthy of being called a blessed tree. And since the branches of purely intellectual thoughts are abstracted from the accidents of bodies, it is fitting that it be neither eastern nor western. As for the fifth, which is the prophetic holy faculty, it is at the utmost of nobility and purity, for the discursive faculty divides into that which needs instruction and that which does not need it. There must be the existence of this division to prevent an infinite regress; so it is fitting that this division be described, for its perfection and attributes, as one whose oil almost gives light even if no fire touches it. Thus this example corresponds to these divisions. These lights are arranged one upon another: sense is the first, and it is like a prelude to imagination, and imagination is like a prelude to the intellect. The words of al-Ghazali, may God Most High have mercy on him, as transmitted by al-Isfahani in his tafsir from him, end here. And God knows best.

Since, on the basis of what preceded concerning the attribute of the divine spirit, the meaning is ﹙so We guided you by it﹚, He connected to it His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed you guide﴾, that is, you clarify and direct, and He emphasized it because of their denial of that, ﴿to a path﴾, that is, a very clear road, and even if you toil in explanation with effort on your own part and through intermediaries, as the transitive use with ﹙ila﹚ conveys, it is understood from this that He guides to the path without that exertion for whomever God makes his affair easy, and guides to the path one who is of even greater success than that, ﴿straight﴾, that is, of very firm uprightness, because it is as if it intends to make itself upright; so after its uprightness exists it preserves it from the slightest deficiency. It is every quality that it calls to among the traits of this upright religion, which is the creed of Abraham, upon him be prayers and peace. Then He replaced it with a substitute, magnifying its status, His saying, a substitute of the whole for the whole, a definite noun from an indefinite one, shifting the speech from the locus of majesty to one greater than it, indicating the grandeur of this path by what it contains of the comprehensive mercy and retribution, as encouragement and warning:

Sirat Allah (the path of Allah): that is, the Greatest King, who combines all the attributes of perfection. Then He described Himself as the owner of what He opened this discourse by stating, that the kingdom belongs to Him, saying: ﴿To Him belongs﴾ the dominion of ﴿whatever is in the heavens﴾, that is, all the heavens which are beneath His Throne, and the earth, because it is within the heavens, and whatever is in them of meanings and entities, ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾.

When He, glorified be He, informed that He is the originator of all things and the owner of the realms of the unseen (ghayb) and the witnessed (shahadah), of creation and command, and that He alone possesses all greatness, and it was fixed in minds and implanted in natural dispositions (fitrah) that whoever initiates something, having no equal, is able to restore it and that the return of all his affairs is to Him, therefore the outcome of all that preceded was, by way of addressing those who deny this, promises and threats for the people of obedience and disobedience, on the basis of what is implied: how can He possess what was mentioned on a lasting basis, when we see for others many things that are attributed to them and whose disposal and management are held in their hands? ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah﴾, that is, the One who encompasses all attributes of perfection, who is exalted above any likeness or equal, and He is the Great, the Exalted, not to anyone other than Him, ﴿do affairs return﴾, that is, on a lasting basis, even though they appear to be in the possession of others, such that the ignorant one thinks their possession is firmly his. Abu Hayyan said: He informed with the present tense, and what is meant by it is continuity, like the saying: Zayd gives and withholds, meaning that it is his custom to do so, and not the literal sense of the future. ﴿The affairs﴾, that is, all of them, of creation and command, are manifest in meaning and in a hidden sense in this world through what He has appointed of rulers and placed among people of means (asbab); and clear in what lies beyond them, since He, alone, cut off all of that, the Mighty, the Wise, the Most High, the Most Great.

Thus the end of the surah has returned to its beginning, its joints have bent back to what connects them, and it is linked, in that it is in the revelation that guides, at the beginning of az-Zukhruf, in the most complete manner of this luminous Book, with the endings in it connected to the openings and the scents to the morning clouds. And Allah knows best what is correct.
